 Max Still Image Resolution: 48MP
 Max Video Resolution: 4K at 60fps
 Stabilization: 3-Axis gimbal
Why I Think It’s Great:
The DJI Mini 3 Pro is another powerful drone that’s lightweight and easy to carry. At just 249 grams, it’s
light enough to avoid extra registration in most countries. Despite its compact size, it offers features that
make it feel like a professional tool.
The 48MP camera allows you to take high-quality photos with lots of detail. The 4K video at 60 frames/
second lets you record smooth and clear footage, whether you’re capturing landscapes or fast-moving
scenes. The 3-axis gimbal helps keep the camera steady, even if there’s some wind.
With 34 minutes of flight time (or up to 47 minutes with an extended battery), you have plenty of time
to capture your shots. Plus, the OcuSync 3.0 system gives you a strong connection, even when flying up
to 12 kilometers away.
You’ll also appreciate the obstacle avoidance feature, which helps prevent crashes, and the return-to-
home function that brings the drone back safely if the battery runs low or it loses signal.

The vertical shooting mode is also great for social media content, as it allows for portrait shots without
needing to crop the image later.
Features and Specifications:
 A 48-megapixel camera that captures stunning 4K/60fps videos and high-quality images.
 It can cover up to 34 minutes of flight time and up to 12 kilometers.
 The 3-axis gimbal and advanced obstacle sensors keep your flight steady and smooth. The drone
can sense obstacles in front, behind, and below, which helps prevent crashes.
 Easy-to-use remote control for smooth navigation.
 Intelligent features like QuickShots, ActiveTrack, and GPS make flying and capturing videos
effortless.
 Weighing just 249g, it’s perfect for travel and easy to carry.
Pros:
 Easy to fly, thanks to its intelligent features and simple controls.
 The 48MP camera delivers beautiful photos and videos in high resolution.
 Long 34-minute flight time, giving you more time in the air to capture amazing shots.
 Lightweight and portable design, great for taking on the go.
 Obstacle detection and safety features provide a more stable and safe flying experience.
Cons:
 The drone only has sensors for the front, back, and bottom, so it can’t detect obstacles from the
sides.
 Limited to 2.4GHz and 5GHz transmission frequencies, which might not work well in every
location.
Price and Availability:
You can buy the DJI Mini 3 Pro on the official DJI website or at authorized stores. Prices range from $719
to $838, depending on the bundle and accessories included.
The DJI Mini 3 Pro is a fantastic choice for beginners, thanks to its advanced features, high-quality
camera, and easy-to-use design.
While it has some limitations with obstacle detection, it still offers a great experience for anyone looking
for a reliable, portable drone.

4). DJI FPV

 Weight: 795 g
 Flight Time: Up to 20 minutes
 Maximum Flying Distance: 10 km (FCC)
 Max Video Resolution: 4K at 60fps
 Stabilization: RockSteady electronic image stabilization
 Field of View (FOV): 150 degrees
Why I Think It’s Great:
For anyone who wants an exciting flying experience, the DJI FPV is the best beginner drone for this, and I
definitely recommend it.
It offers a first-person view (FPV), so when you wear the FPV goggles, it feels like you’re in the cockpit.
The 150-degree wide-angle view is incredible, giving you a full, immersive perspective while flying.
With its 4K video resolution at 60fps, the footage is super clear and detailed, making it great for both fast
racing and scenic flights.
Even at high speeds, the RockSteady stabilization keeps your videos smooth. The drone also comes with
a 20-minute flight time, which is pretty solid for an FPV drone, and it’s much longer than many others in
its category.
The OcuSync 3.0 transmission system ensures that you have a strong video signal, even when flying far—
up to 10 kilometers. This gives you a lot of freedom to explore without losing connection.
It’s surprisingly friendly for beginners, thanks to its Normal mode, which stabilizes the flight and adds
GPS to make flying easier.

It also has safety features like obstacle sensors at the front and bottom, and a return-to-home function in
case the signal is lost or the battery gets low. These are great for avoiding accidents while flying.
If you’re looking for speed, the Manual mode lets you go all out with flips, rolls, and fast maneuvers,
reaching up to 97 mph.
Features and Specifications:
 You can choose between Normal, Sport, or Manual mode, depending on your flying experience.
Normal mode is easy for beginners, while Manual offers full control for advanced users.
 The 4K camera captures sharp, high-quality footage at 60 frames per second. You can also record
slow-motion at 1080p with up to 120 frames per second, making it great for action shots.
 A 150-degree wide-angle view gives you an immersive flying experience, allowing you to see
more of your surroundings.
 With up to 20 minutes of flight time and a range of up to 10km, you can fly far and capture
stunning footage without worrying about losing signal.
 Built-in obstacle sensors help detect barriers in front and below the drone, helping to prevent
crashes.
Pros:
 Easy to fly with intuitive controls, making it a great choice for beginners.
 Captures stunning 4K videos with sharp detail and rich colors.
 The obstacle avoidance system helps ensure a safer flight by preventing collisions.
 The three different flight modes offer flexibility, so you can adjust based on your skill level.
 With a range of up to 10km, you can explore more areas without worrying about losing
connection.
Cons:
 It’s a bit expensive compared to other beginner drones.
 The flight time is limited to around 20 minutes, which may feel short for longer flights.
 Its weight makes it less portable than some lighter drones, so it might not be ideal for quick
setups.
Price and availability:
The DJI FPV Combo with Goggles V2 is priced at $698, making it a great choice if you’re ready to start
flying FPV.
If you’re looking for a more advanced setup, the DJI FPV Explorer Combo with Goggles Integra comes in
at $999, offering some extra features for those who want to take their experience up a notch. Both are
great options, depending on what you’re after!
Ultimately, the DJI FPV is the perfect drone for any beginner looking to invest in quality and ease of use.
Though it may come with an expensive price tag and be heavier than other drones, its worth cannot be
overlooked.

5). DJI Mini SE

 Weight: 249 g
 Dimensions: Folded: 138×81×58 mm | Unfolded: 159×203×56 mm
 Max Flight Time: 30 minutes
 Maximum Flying Distance: 4 km
 Max Still Image Resolution: 12MP
 Max Video Resolution: 2.7K at 30fps
 Stabilization: 3-Axis gimbal
Why I Think It’s Great:
Weighing just 249 grams, the DJI Mini SE is light and easy to carry, making it great for travel or capturing
everyday moments. Despite its small size, it’s loaded with features that make flying simple and
enjoyable.
The 2.7K video resolution allows you to capture clear and detailed footage, which is great for those who
want quality without needing high-end equipment.
The 3-axis gimbal keeps your camera stable, even if there’s some wind, ensuring your videos remain
smooth and your photos sharp, even if you’re still learning how to fly the drone.
With 30 minutes of flight time, the Mini SE gives you plenty of time to explore and capture great shots
before needing a recharge. While it doesn’t have 4K video like some higher-end models, the 2.7K
resolution is more than enough for most casual users.
Plus, it supports QuickShots, which includes automated camera movements like "Rocket" and "Circle" to
help beginners capture cinematic footage with ease.
One standout feature is its maximum flight range—up to 4 km in CE regions and 10 km in FCC regions,
giving you the ability to travel farther and capture footage from a distance, all while staying connected
through a reliable video feed.

And if something goes wrong, the return-to-home feature kicks in, automatically bringing the drone back
to you when the battery gets low or it loses signal.
Features and Specifications:
 It is a lightweight drone
 It has a camera resolution of 12MP that can shoot 2.7K video at 30fps
 It features a 3-axis motorized gimbal that provides stability to the camera during flight.
 A flight distance of 2.5 miles within 30 minutes.
 The exceptional DJI Mini SE has GPS, altitude holds, and vision sensors that allow it to remain
stationary mid-air, retain the same height, and circumvent objects.
 It can also perform automated flight maneuvers such as Dronie, Rocket, Circle, Helix, and
QuickShot modes.
 The app can control your drone, stream live footage, or edit photos and videos.
Pros:
 Lightweight and compact design
 Easy to use and beginner-friendly
 Good camera quality with 2.7K video resolution
 Long flight time of up to 30 minutes
 Features GPS, vision sensors, and altitude hold for stable flight
 Automated flight modes for creative shots
 Affordable price point
Cons:
 No obstacle avoidance sensors on the sides or back of the drone
 Limited camera control options compared to more advanced DJI drones
 No 4K video recording capability
Price and Availability:
The DJI Mini SE offers an affordable entry point into aerial photography. Priced around $299, it is
available through DJI’s official website and authorized retailers like Amazon.
This drone is an excellent value for its features, making it a great option for those looking to capture
high-quality footage without spending a fortune.

6). DJI Mavic Air 2

 Weight: 570 g
 Dimensions: Folded: 180×97×84 mm | Unfolded: 183×253×77 mm
 Max Flight Time: 34 minutes
 Maximum Flying Distance: 10 km
 Max Still Image Resolution: 48MP
 Max Video Resolution: 4K at 60fps
 Stabilization: 3-Axis gimbal
Why I Think It’s Great:
This is a compact drone that stands out for its impressive balance of portability and high performance.
The DJI Mavic Air 2 has a 48MP camera that delivers detailed photos, and the ability to record 4K video
at 60fps is perfect for capturing smooth, high-quality footage.
With the 34-minute flight time, you get plenty of air time to film uninterrupted, whether you're shooting
scenic landscapes or fast-moving subjects.
With a range of up to 10 km, you can fly far while maintaining a stable connection, thanks to the
OcuSync 2.0 system.
One of the standout features for me is the FocusTrack system, which includes ActiveTrack for following
moving subjects and Spotlight, which keeps the camera focused on a subject while you fly without any
restrictions.

It also has obstacle avoidance sensors to help prevent crashes, making flying safer and more reliable.
Features and Specifications:
 1/2-inch CMOS sensor paired with a 3-axis gimbal for stable footage.
 It captures 48MP photos and records 4K video at 60fps, giving you high-quality shots.
 Maximum flight time is up to 34 minutes, and you can reach a top speed of 42.5 mph.
 The drone has a signal range of up to 6.2 miles (10 km), using the OcuSync 2.0 transmission
system.
 It includes obstacle avoidance technology to avoid collisions, with sensors covering forward,
backward, and downward directions.
 You can use features like QuickShot, ActiveTrack, and SmartPhoto through the DJI Fly app,
making capturing footage easy.
Pros:
 The camera and gimbal offer top-notch image and video quality.
 Long flight time of 34 minutes allows for extended use.
 Obstacle avoidance ensures a safer flying experience.
 The DJI Fly app is simple to use, even for beginners.
Cons:
 It’s more expensive compared to other entry-level drones.
 The controller doesn’t have a built-in display.
 Its small size can make it more vulnerable to wind.
Price and Availability:
The DJI Mavic Air 2 is available for around $559 on the DJI website and from other retailers. It’s a great
choice for those looking for a feature-rich drone with excellent performance. With the Mavic Air 2, you
will surely get your money's worth!

7). DJI Phantom 4 RTK

 Weight: 1391 g
 Dimensions: Diagonal Distance: 350 mm
 Max Flight Time: About 30 minutes
 Max Speed: 36 mph (58 kph) in Sport Mode
 Max Transmission Range: 7 km (FCC)
 Camera: 20MP, 1-inch sensor, 4K video at 30fps
 Stabilization: 3-axis gimbal for smooth video
 Obstacle Avoidance: Sensors at the front, rear, and bottom to prevent crashes
 Positioning: RTK system for pinpoint accuracy
 Intelligent Flight Modes: QuickShot, ActiveTrack, and TapFly for easy flying and tracking
Why I Think It’s Great:
The DJI Phantom 4 RTK is not just another drone—it's built specifically for professionals who need
pinpoint accuracy in their aerial data.
With the RTK module, it achieves centimeter-level precision, which is critical for industries like surveying
and mapping. This reduces the need for Ground Control Points (GCPs), helping save time and making the
work faster.
The 1-inch CMOS sensor helps you take professional-quality photos and videos. Its 20-megapixel camera
gives you clear, high-resolution images, and the mechanical shutter prevents distortion when the drone
is moving.
The long 30-minute flight time is a big plus, especially when you need to cover large areas, while the
obstacle avoidance system ensures you can fly with confidence, especially in tight spaces.

For professionals in industries like agriculture, real estate, and construction, the DJI Phantom 4 RTK
stands out as a tool that offers both precision and ease of use, making it an excellent investment for
accurate aerial mapping.
Features and Specifications:
 1-inch CMOS sensor with a 20-megapixel camera for high-quality aerial photos and videos.
 Flight time of up to 30 minutes, and can fly at speeds up to 72 km/h.
 Signal transmission range of 7 km, allowing for longer-distance flights.
 Equipped with an RTK module, providing centimeter-level accuracy for precise mapping and
surveying.
 The remote controller has an integrated screen, making it easy to control and view live footage
in real time.
Pros:
 The RTK module ensures precise mapping and is ideal for professionals in fields like construction,
agriculture, and surveying.
 Easy to set up and operate, making it user-friendly for capturing high-quality footage.
 The remote controller’s integrated tablet simplifies the flying process, offering real-time footage
and control.
Cons:
 The price is quite high, so it may not be affordable for everyone.
 It’s a bit bulky, which makes it harder to carry around compared to smaller drones.
Price and Availability:
The DJI Phantom 4 RTK is available on the official DJI website and through authorized retailers. It retails
at around $7,9750.
Although it’s on the pricier side, its advanced features make it an incredible investment for professionals
in industries requiring precise aerial mapping and surveying.
And there you have it!
These are the seven best drones I highly recommend for every beginner.
Tips for First-Time Flyers
Now, you’ve got your first drone, and you’re ready to take it for a spin.
Flying a drone is so interesting, but there are a few things you should know to make your experience
safer and more enjoyable.
Let’s go through some helpful tips that will make your first drone flight a smooth one.
a). Start Low and Slow
It’s tempting to shoot your drone up high and fly fast right away, but it’s better to take it slow at first. Fly
at a low height in a big, open space where there’s nothing around to crash into.

A park or field is perfect for this. This way, you can practice without worrying about hitting trees,
buildings, or power lines.
Begin with simple moves like hovering in place, flying straight, and making gentle turns. Getting used to
the basic controls will help you feel more comfortable when you want to try flying higher or faster.
b). Know the Rules
Before you fly, make sure you’re in a spot where it’s allowed. Some places have rules about where
drones can be flown, like near airports or in crowded areas. If your drone is over a certain weight, you
may even need to register it.
It’s also important to keep your drone within sight while flying.
Even if you’re using FPV drones (drones where you fly with goggles that give you a first-person view), it’s
a good idea to have someone nearby watching the drone so you don’t lose track of it.
c). Get Comfortable with the Controls
Learning how to control your drone is key. Most controllers have two sticks: one moves the drone up and
down and spins it around; the other moves it forward, backward, and side to side.
At first, the controls may feel strange, but with some practice, they’ll become second nature.
Start with basic moves, like flying in a straight line or hovering in one spot. Don’t rush into complicated
tricks—just focus on keeping the drone steady. Some drones even have a beginner mode that limits
speed and height to help you learn.
d). Keep an Eye on Battery Life
Batteries don’t last long in drones—usually around 20 to 30 minutes. It’s important to know how much
time you have left before the battery runs out. You don’t want your drone dropping out of the sky
because the battery died.
Some drones have a feature that automatically brings them back when the battery is low. This return-to-
home feature is super helpful, especially if you’re still getting used to flying.
e). Stay Calm While Flying
It’s easy to get nervous when you’re flying a drone for the first time, but staying calm is important. If
your drone starts moving too fast or in the wrong direction, make small, gentle adjustments to the
controls. Don’t jerk the sticks too much or panic.
A good tip is to practice hovering. Keeping the drone still in one spot helps you get used to controlling it
without overreacting. The more relaxed you are, the better you’ll fly.
f). Watch for Obstacles
Even in an open space, always be aware of what’s around you. Look out for trees, power lines, or other
people. Crashing into things is not only bad for your drone but could be dangerous for others, too.

Some drones have sensors that help them avoid obstacles, but it’s still best to be careful. Rely on your
eyes and good judgment.
e). Pay Attention to the Weather
Weather affects how drones fly.
Strong winds, rain, or even extreme heat can mess with how your drone handles. Before you fly, check
the weather. A calm, sunny day is perfect for flying. On windy days, your drone might be harder to
control, especially if it’s lightweight.
f). Take It Step by Step
Don’t rush the process. Flying a drone is something you’ll get better at with time and practice.
Start with simple moves and build your skills slowly. Once you feel more confident, you can try more
advanced tricks or fly in tighter spaces.
With FPV drones, you might feel disoriented when you first use the goggles, but that’s normal. Take your
time and get comfortable with the controls before trying anything complex.
Ready to Take Flight? Here’s My Final Thought
So, that’s my list of the best DJI drones for beginners.
If you're itching to get in the air, any of these seven picks will have you flying with confidence in no time.
These seven models offer the perfect mix of easy controls and impressive features, helping you get the
hang of things without feeling overwhelmed.
It doesn’t matter if you're capturing cool aerial footage or just enjoying the flight experience; these
drones are great for any first-timer.
They have everything you need for easy takeoffs and safe landings. So, pick your favorite, hit the skies,
and enjoy the view—just keep an eye out for those trees!
Once you start flying, you'll be hooked for sure.

title: How to Rank Higher on Google Maps in Nigeria
content:
How to Rank Higher on Google Maps in Nigeria
“Want to know how to rank higher on Google Maps in Nigeria? Follow these easy steps to boost your
business and attract more customers!”
Your Google Maps listing is a powerful tool for your business. It helps new customers find you, makes
you stand out from competitors, and drives more business—all for free.
But these benefits only come if your listing is highly visible. Just because your business is listed in an area
doesn’t mean Google will automatically rank it high for searches in that area.
For businesses in Nigeria, a high Google Maps ranking is very important.
Let’s say you have a bakery in Ikeja. When people search for "best bread in Ikeja," you want your bakery
to pop up first, just like in this picture.

A top-ranking listing can make your business a local favorite, bringing in more customers and increasing
your sales.
In this guide on how to rank higher on Google Maps in Nigeria, I'll show you simple steps to improve
your Google Maps listing so you'll get more visibility and attract more customers right to your door.
Let's get started and make your business the top choice on Google Maps!
Common Challenges Faced By Businesses in Nigeria
Running a business in Nigeria has its own set of challenges, especially when it comes to getting noticed
on Google Maps.
Let’s look at some common problems that you might have faced also.

Local SEO Struggles
a). Facing Tough Competition
The local market is very competitive. Whether you own a small boutique in Lagos or a tech store in
Abuja, you're up against many other businesses trying to attract the same customers.
Standing out isn’t easy, and you need to make sure your Google Maps listing and your website are in
great shape.
b). Missing or Incorrect Business Information
Imagine someone trying to find your business but ending up at the wrong address because your Google
Maps information is outdated or incorrect.
This not only frustrates potential customers but also makes you look unprofessional.
It’s crucial to keep your business name, address, and phone number (NAP) consistent across all online
platforms. An outdated or incorrect listing can turn away potential customers.
c). Keeping Business Details Up-to-Date
Businesses change, and so do their details. Maybe you’ve changed your operating hours, moved to a
new location, or started offering new services.
It's important to update this information on your Google Maps listing and your website. Keeping these
details current ensures that customers can always find the right information when they need it.
What Do Customers Want?
a). Quick Access to Local Businesses
Customers want to find local businesses quickly and easily. They don’t have time to sift through outdated
information or search endlessly for your contact details.
They expect to find everything they need in one place, and they expect it to be accurate. If your
information isn’t readily available or is incorrect, they might look elsewhere.
b). Accurate Directions, Reviews, and Contact Information
People rely heavily on Google Maps for accurate directions, honest reviews, and up-to-date contact
information.
I once worked with a plumbing service in Centreville that faced similar issues.
Their business listing had incorrect information, leading potential customers to the wrong location and
causing frustration.
After fixing their address and optimizing their Google Business Profile, they quickly climbed to the #1
spot for "Centreville Plumber."


This not only increased their visibility but also boosted their credibility.
If your business details are wrong or missing, potential customers might end up going to your
competitor.
Customers want to know exactly where you are, what others think of your business, and how to get in
touch with you quickly. If this information isn’t easily accessible or accurate, you risk losing business.
Recognizing these common problems is the first step to improving your Google Maps ranking and
making your business stand out in Nigeria.
If you can fix these issues, people will find and choose your business more easily.

What Are the Google Maps Ranking Factors?
I've had several businesses come to me, frustrated because they've tried everything they could think of
to get their business to show up higher on Google Maps.
They've updated their business name, address, and phone number, added photos, and even written
detailed descriptions.
But despite all this effort, they still struggle to rank well in local search results. So, let's talk about why
this happens and what factors Google looks at when deciding who ranks where.
a). Google Business Profile (GBP) Optimization
First, let's discuss your Google Business Profile (GBP). Many businesses think that just having a profile is
enough, but that's not the case. Google looks at:
i). Accurate Information
It's crucial to make sure your business name, address, and phone number are consistent everywhere
online. If there are discrepancies, it can confuse Google and your customers.
ii). Right Category
Choosing the most accurate category for your business is essential. It helps Google understand what
your business does and match it with the right searches.
iii). Detailed Description
Writing a clear, keyword-rich description is key. It's not just about telling people what you do but also
about including the words they might use to find businesses like yours.
iv). Photos and Videos
High-quality visuals can make a big difference. They don't just make your profile look better; they can
also help attract more views.
b). Relevance, Distance, and Prominence
Then there are the big three factors Google considers: relevance, distance, and prominence.
i). Relevance
This is about how well your business matches what someone is searching for. If your profile has the right
keywords and categories, you're more likely to appear in relevant searches.
I've seen businesses that perfectly match a search query still not show up because they haven't
optimized for relevance.
ii). Distance
Google looks at how close your business is to the person searching. While you can't change your
location, ensuring your address is accurately listed is crucial.
Sometimes, businesses are just too far from the searcher, which can affect their ranking.

iii). Prominence
This is a measure of how well-known and trusted your business is.
Google looks at things like the number and quality of your reviews, how well-known your business is
online, and your presence in local directories.
Businesses with lots of positive reviews and a strong online presence tend to rank higher.
So, when your business is not ranking as it should, it's often because you haven't fully addressed these
factors. It's not just about being online; it's about being strategically visible.
Setting Up and Optimizing Your Google Business Profile (GBP)
If you want your business to rank higher on Google Maps in Nigeria, it all starts with a great Google
Business Profile (GBP).
This step-by-step guide will walk you through the entire process, from creating your profile to optimizing
your GBP for potential customers.
Let’s start!
Step 1: Sign In or Create a Google Account
First, you need to sign in to your Google account. If you don’t have one, no worries. Creating a Google
account is easy and free. Just head over to the Google sign-up page and follow the instructions.

I will advise you to pick the business account that makes it easier to set up your Google Business Profile.
Step 2: Go to Google My Business
Once you’re signed in, go to the Google My Business page. Click on the “Manage now” button to start
setting up your profile.

Step 3: Enter Your Business Name
Type in your business name.
If it doesn’t pop up in the drop-down list, click on “Create a business with this name.” Make sure to use
the exact name as it appears on your website and other places online.

Step 4: Choose Your Business Category

Pick the category that best describes what you do. This helps Google show your business to people
searching for related services.


When you choose a local store or service business, the first image will display, but if you opt for an online
retail business, the second image will appear.
However, you would still have to input your business category regardless of the option you chose.

Step 5: Add Your Location
If you have a physical store or office, enter your address. This helps customers find you on Google Maps.

Step 6: Enter Your Contact Information
Add your phone number and website URL. This makes it easy for customers to call you or visit your
website.


Step 7: Verify Your Business
Google will ask you to verify your business.
They usually send a postcard with a verification code to your business address. Enter the code in your
Google Business Profile account to verify your profile.

Optimizing Your Google Business Profile
Now that your profile is set up let's make it even better!
Here’s how to do it step by step.
a). Accurate Information
First, ensure all your business information, like your name, address, and phone number (NAP), is correct
and consistent everywhere online. Inconsistent info can confuse customers and harm your ranking.

i). Check and Update Your NAP:
 Log in to your Google Business Profile account.
 Go to the “Info” tab.
 Make sure your business name, address, and phone number are correct and match what’s on
your other listings. Consistency is key, so double-check that all details match everywhere.
ii). Include Your Tracked and Main Number:
If you use call tracking, list your tracked number as the primary phone number and your main number as
the secondary one.
This way, you can monitor the effectiveness of your listing while still having your main number visible to
Google.

b). Claim Your Google Business Profile
Before you can fully optimize your profile, you need to claim it. This gives you control over the
information displayed and allows you to make necessary updates.

i). Claim Your Listing:
 Go to Google.com/maps or open the Google Maps app.
 Search for your business name. If it appears, click on it and select “Claim this business” or “Own
this business?”
 Follow the prompts to verify your ownership. You might receive a postcard with a verification
code, or you may be able to verify by phone or email.
c). Detailed Business Description
Your business description should be clear and detailed. Use keywords that people might search for. For
example, if you run a barbershop, mention “haircuts” and “grooming services.”


i). Write an Engaging Description:
 Go to the “Info” tab in your Google Business Profile dashboard.
 Find the “Add business description” section.
 Write a description that clearly explains what your business does, including important keywords.
ii). Properly Categorize Your Business

 Choose the primary category that best represents your core offering.
 Select additional categories, if applicable, to cover other services you provide.
d). Add Photos and Videos
High-quality photos and videos can make your profile more appealing. Show off your facilities, your staff,
and your services. People are more likely to visit a business that looks inviting.
i). Upload Photos and Videos:

 Go to the “Photos” tab in your Google Business Profile dashboard.
 Add a variety of photos, including your logo, cover photo, and images of your business's interior
and exterior.
 Upload videos showcasing your services or products.
ii). Add Photos Regularly:
Keep your profile fresh by adding new photos frequently. This signals to Google that your business is
active and engaging.

e). Collect and Manage Reviews
Encourage happy customers to leave positive reviews. Reviews are crucial for ranking higher on Google
Maps. Respond to reviews, both good and bad, to show that you care about customer feedback.
i). Gather Reviews:
 Ask satisfied customers to leave a review.
 Create a shareable review link and include it in your email signature or on your website.
ii). Respond to Reviews:

 Log in to your Google Business Profile account.
 Go to the “Reviews” tab.
 Respond to all reviews, thank customers for their feedback, and address any issues raised.
e). Post Regularly
Keep your Google Business Profile active by posting updates, special offers, and news about your
business. Regular posts keep your profile fresh and engaging.
i). Create Posts:
 Go to the “Posts” tab in your Google Business Profile dashboard.
 Write posts about new products, special offers, or any updates about your business.
 Include images and links to make your posts more engaging.
f). Utilize Insights
Google provides insights on how customers interact with your profile. Use this data to see what works
and what doesn’t. Adjust your strategy based on these insights to improve your presence.
1). Check Insights:
 Go to the “Insights” tab in your Google Business Profile dashboard.

 Review data on how customers find your profile, what actions they take, and other engagement
metrics.
 Use this information to refine your GBP strategy.
ii). Keep Your Hours Updated:
 Regularly update your business hours, including special hours for holidays. This helps customers
know when you’re open and improves your reliability.
iii). Consolidate Your Listings:
 Make sure you don’t have duplicate listings on Google Maps. Consolidate any duplicates to
ensure your true listing ranks higher.
By following these steps, you'll be well on your way to optimizing your Google Business Profile and
attracting more customers through local search.
How to Gather and Manage GBP Reviews
When you're running a business in Nigeria, getting good reviews on your Google Business Profile (GBP)
can make a big difference.
It's like when people talk about a great place they've visited; suddenly, everyone wants to check it out.
Here’s how to get and manage reviews and handle fake ones.
a). Encourage Customers to Leave Reviews
One of the best ways to get positive reviews is to ask your happy customers directly. Here’s how you can
do it:
i). Ask in Person:
 After providing a good service or selling a product, ask your customers to leave a review on your
GBP. For instance, if you run a dry cleaning service, ask clients if they could share their
experience online.
ii). Use SMS or WhatsApp:
 Send a thank-you message to your customers with a link to your Google Business Profile, asking
them to leave a review. This is quick and easy for them.
iii). Email Requests:
 If you have an email list, send follow-up emails asking for reviews. Include a direct link to your
GBP to make it simple.
b). Respond to Reviews
Engaging with your reviews shows that you care about customer feedback, whether it’s positive or
negative.

i). Thank Positive Reviewers:
 A simple “Thank you for your kind words!” goes a long way. It shows appreciation and
encourages others to leave positive reviews.
ii). Address Negative Reviews:
 Be professional and polite. Apologize if necessary and offer to resolve the issue. This shows
potential customers that you are committed to good service.
c). Handle Fake Reviews
Fake reviews can harm your business, so it’s important to address them promptly.
i). Report the Review:
 If you find a fake review, go to your GBP dashboard, find the review, and click “Flag as
inappropriate.” Google will review your report and take action if the review breaks their rules.
ii). Respond to the Review:
 If the review is not removed, respond to it professionally. You can reply politely, saying, "We
can’t seem to recall this incident. We're here to help sort out any issues, though!"
This helps show potential customers that the review is not genuine.
c). Share Positive Reviews
Highlighting positive reviews can attract more customers.
i). Social Media:
 Share screenshots of positive reviews on your social media pages. This showcases your good
reputation to a broader audience.
ii). Website Testimonials:
 Add positive reviews to a testimonials section on your website. This builds trust with new
visitors.
Handling your reviews is all about connecting with your customers and building a community that trusts
what you do.
Keep your responses honest, respectful, and professional. This approach will not only help your business
look good but also feel like a trusted spot in the community.
How to Use Citations and Local Listings to Grow Your Business
What exactly are citations?
Citations are mentions of your business name, address, and phone number (NAP) on other websites.
These mentions help boost your local SEO, making it easier for people to find your business on Google
Maps.

The more consistent and widespread your citations, the more Google trusts your business information,
which helps improve your ranking.
This increases your ranking on Google Maps and increases your visibility, driving more traffic to your
business.
Now, let me share a quick story. I had a client with a limo service who wanted to rank for the keyword
"limousine service near Logan Airport."
Despite offering excellent services, they weren't getting noticed. I listed their business in relevant local
directories and made sure their NAP information was consistent everywhere.
Within six weeks, their business climbed to the #1 spot on Google Maps.


Now, let’s talk about how you can make this work for your business.

a). List Your Business in Local Directories
Getting listed in local directories is crucial. It helps Google recognize your business as legitimate and
boosts your local SEO.
You should list your business on popular Nigerian directories like VConnect, BusinessList Nigeria, and
ConnectNigeria. People often use these sites to find local services.
b). Use Local SEO Techniques
Using local SEO techniques can significantly boost your visibility on Google Maps. Start by researching
local keywords relevant to your area and services.
For instance, if you run a tailoring service in Abuja, use keywords like “affordable tailoring in Abuja.”
Creating content about local events, news, or activities on your website can also engage local customers
and help your website rank for local searches.
c). Build Local Backlinks
Backlinks from reputable local sites can boost your SEO. Reach out to local bloggers to write about your
business or include you in their listings.
Participating in local events and getting mentioned on their websites also helps.
Using citations and local listings can really put your business on the map in Nigeria. It's about making
sure when people search for what you offer, your business pops up first.
If managing all this feels overwhelming, don't hesitate to reach out to experts who can help you achieve
these results.
How to Track Performance and Make Improvements
Getting your business on Google Maps is just the start. Once you're up and running, the real work
begins: tracking how well you're doing and finding ways to do even better.
Here's how you can do this:
a). Check Out Google My Business Insights
Start with Google My Business Insights. This feature shows you how customers find your listing—
whether they searched directly for your business or stumbled upon it while looking for something else.
Knowing this helps you understand what's working and where you might need to make some changes.
b). Monitor Customer Interactions
Pay attention to how customers interact with your listing. Look at how many people call your business
directly from your profile or use the map to find directions to your place.
This will tell you if your contact information is clear and helpful. If you're not seeing much activity,
consider updating your details to make them more straightforward or more visible.

c). Respond to Reviews
Reviews are a key part of your Google Maps listing. Regularly read and respond to them.
Say thanks to those who leave positive reviews and address any concerns raised by less satisfied
customers.
This doesn't just show that you value feedback. It also helps you identify areas for improvement.
d). Use Additional Tools
For a deeper analysis, consider using tools like SEMrush or Moz Local. These can give you a detailed view
of your search rankings and help you track changes over time.
They offer insights that can guide your efforts to improve your SEO and get better results from your
Google Maps listing.
Keeping an eye on your Google Maps performance isn't just about spotting changes. It's about finding
new ways to connect with potential customers and making your business easy to find and interact with.
So, regularly update your information, respond to customer reviews, and use the right tools to track your
progress.
By doing this, you'll not only stay visible but also become more appealing to those searching online.
Case Studies: Two Nigerian Businesses' Google Maps Journey
Let's look at how two local businesses in Nigeria have fared with their Google Maps strategies—one
soared, and the other stumbled.
I will share their stories to give you an idea of what happened.
a). Egac Web Hosting
Egac Web Hosting wasn’t very well known until they really focused on their Google Maps presence. They
came to me because they wanted to rank higher on Google.
They were struggling with visibility despite having great services and customer reviews.
Here’s how we turned things around for them:
i). Accurate Business Information:
We ensured all their business information was accurate and consistent. This included their name,
address, phone number, and website. Having the correct details helped Google trust their listing more.
ii). Engaging Photos and Videos:
We added high-quality photos and videos showcasing their office, staff, and some behind-the-scenes
action. This made their profile more appealing and trustworthy to potential customers.
iii). Regular Posts:
Posting updates, special offers, and news about their services kept their profile active. This not only
informed customers but also signaled to Google that the business was active and engaging.

iv). Customer Reviews:
Encouraging satisfied customers to leave positive reviews was a game-changer. Egac Web Hosting saw an
increase in positive feedback, which boosted their credibility and ranking.

After some months of working with me on Google Maps, this resulted in more traffic and customers
finding them easily.
b). Cartoon Maker Specialist

I’ve been following the progress of Cartoon Maker Specialist, a graphic design business in Ota, for a while
now. Initially, they were ranking well, but recently, they experienced a drop in their position. Here’s what
happened:
a). Profile Inactivity:
They stopped posting regular updates and engaging with their customers. This inactivity led to a drop in
their ranking as Google favors active listings.
b). Inconsistent Information:
Their business information wasn’t updated regularly, which caused confusion and reduced their
credibility.
c). Fewer Reviews:
They weren’t encouraging enough customer reviews. This lack of engagement made their profile less
attractive compared to competitors.
To help them regain their ranking, I started by updating their business information and ensuring it was
consistent across all platforms.
I also encouraged them to post regular updates and engage more with their customers. Slowly but
surely, they’re climbing back up the rankings.
This is where they stand now:


If you’re also struggling with your Google Maps ranking, these stories show that simple, consistent
efforts can make a big difference.
Are You Ready To Put In the Work?
Getting your business noticed on Google Maps in Nigeria doesn’t have to be hard.
First, keep your info right and up-to-date. If your address, phone number, or hours change, update them
right away.
Add good photos and videos. Show what your place looks like and what you offer. It makes your profile
more appealing.
Ask happy customers for reviews. Thank them and respond to the not-so-happy ones, too. This shows
you care and builds trust.
Post updates regularly. Tell people about new products, special offers, or events happening at your
business.
Check how you’re doing. Use Google My Business Insights to see what works and what doesn’t. Make
changes based on this info.
Doing these things can make a big difference. Your customers are looking for you. Make sure they can
find you easily.
If managing all this feels like too much, you can always achieve faster results by working with an expert.
They can help you optimize your profile and get your business to the top.
Start today, and watch your business climb to the top! Your customers are out there; make it easy for
them to find you.

title: SEO Tips to Remember When Building Quality Backlinks
content:
SEO Tips to Remember When Building Quality Backlinks
“Quality backlinks can make all the difference. Follow these SEO tips to remember when building links
that help your site stand out and rank higher effortlessly.”
Building backlinks isn’t just about throwing your website link out there and hoping for the best. It’s like
building relationships—stronger links can actually increase your website’s reputation and rankings.
The value of backlinks depends on the quality, not the quantity. Quality backlinks prove to search
engines that your content is useful and trustworthy, and that’s how you rank higher.
In this post, I’ll share some SEO tips to remember when building high-quality backlinks. These are easy to
follow and will guide you in building strong links for your site.
By the end, you’ll know what makes a backlink valuable and how to build it properly.
Keep reading to find out more!
1). Start with Relevant Content
If you want to build backlinks, your content has to be linkable. No one will share something that doesn’t
provide value, right?
That’s why starting with relevant content is one of the SEO tips to remember. When you create content
that people actually want to read and share, backlinks will follow.
So, how do you make your content stand out and get backlinks?
 Make it useful: Share tips, insights, or solutions to real problems. Content that solves a problem
or answers a question is more likely to get shared.
 Use visuals: Infographics are great for breaking down complicated info into something easy to
understand and share.
 Do your research: Original research or case studies will get attention.
Here’s a simple tip: keep your audience in mind at all times. If your content makes them go, “Oh, I need
this,” you’re already halfway there.
When your content speaks to their needs, it’s more likely to get backlinks from blogs, forums, and social
media.
Creating high-quality content isn’t just about quantity—it’s about offering something of value.
2). Build Relationships in Your Niche
When it comes to getting backlinks, relationships matter. The idea is simple: people will link to your
content if they know and trust you.
That’s why networking with influencers and peers in your niche is one of the backlink tips to remember.
You’re not looking for quick links; you’re building long-term relationships.
So, how do you make these connections?

 Guest blogging: Contact websites in your field and offer to write for them. For example, if you’re
a marketing agency College Station, offering expert insights on digital marketing in your area can
open doors.
 Collaborations: Partner with someone in your niche. A joint webinar, interview, or even a shared
blog post can create backlink opportunities.
 Personalize your outreach: Instead of sending the same message to everyone, take the time to
personalize your approach. Mention a specific article you liked or point out something unique
about their site.
The goal is to add value to their content and get a backlink in return. Relationships take time, but when
done right, they can lead to powerful backlinks that will help grow your site’s authority over time.
Remember, people link to people, not just websites!
3). Focus on Authority Sites
Getting backlinks from authority sites is one of the backlink tips to remember. Search engines trust these
high-ranking sites, so a backlink from them will increase your credibility and help your site rank higher.
So, how do you find authority sites? Look for sites with high domain authority (DA). You can use tools
such as Ahrefs or Moz to check a website’s DA score.
The higher the score, the more valuable a backlink from that site will be. For example, a backlink from a
well-known news site like Forbes or an industry leader’s blog can do wonders for your SEO.
Here are a few steps to pitch your content:
 Do your research: Before you pitch, make sure your content aligns with the site’s audience. For
example, if you’re pitching a tech blog, your content should be about the latest trends or
innovations in technology.
 Personalize your pitch: Don’t send generic emails. Mention specific articles or posts from their
site and tell them how your content will be helpful to their readers.
 Be clear about what you offer: Highlight how your article will be relevant and helpful to their
readers, making it easier for them to say yes.
Building relationships with these authority sites takes time, but it’s worth the effort when you see the
results in your rankings.
3). Leverage Broken Link Building
Broken link building helps you get good backlinks, and it’s easier than you think. Essentially, you’re
helping other websites by pointing out broken links on their pages and offering your content as a
replacement.
It’s a win-win: they fix their broken link, and you get a backlink. This is one of the backlink tips to
remember for anyone looking to improve their link-building game.
To find broken links, you can make use of tools such as Ahrefs, Screaming Frog, or Check My Links (a
Chrome extension).

These tools scan websites for broken links that need fixing. Once you find a broken link that matches the
content you’ve already written or are willing to write, you’re ready to make your move.
Here are a few tips to make your outreach email successful:
 Keep it simple: Let the site owner know about the broken link in a polite way. Don’t
overcomplicate your message.
 Offer value: Mention you have similar content that can replace the broken link. Make it easy for
them by including a link to your content.
 Be specific: Make sure to mention where you found the broken link so they don’t have to search
for it.
Broken link building is a great way to grow your backlink profile. And always follow the SEO starter guide
to do it right!
4). Use Guest Blogging to Your Advantage
Guest blogging is one of the best SEO tips to remember when you're working on building quality
backlinks.
By writing for other websites in your niche, you can reach a new audience, increase your credibility, and
get a valuable backlink to your own site. But there’s a right way to do it.
To start, you’ll need to find blogs that accept guest posts. Look for high-traffic blogs in your industry. You
can search Google for terms like “write for us” or check out websites like AllTop, which lists popular
blogs by category.
Once you’ve found a blog take time to review their content so you can craft a pitch that resonates.
Here are a few tips for guest blogging content:
 Tailor your content: Make sure your article fits the tone and style of the blog you’re writing for. If
they focus on actionable advice, provide step-by-step tips.
 Include value for their audience: Always put what will benefit their readers first. This increases
the chance your post will be accepted and shared.
 Don’t be too promotional: Don’t make your guest post about your product or services. Instead,
provide useful information.
The biggest mistake in guest blogging is treating it like free advertising. The goal is to offer value while
building relationships, not just getting a backlink.
6). Don’t Forget Local Backlinks
When you’re targeting a local audience, local backlinks are super valuable.
It’s one of those SEO tips to remember that can help increase your local search rankings and build trust
with your nearby customers.
Here’s how to leverage local backlinks:

 Connect with local influencers: Reach out to local bloggers, business owners, or community
leaders. For example, if you own a small café, getting featured by a local food blogger or
community website can bring in new customers and boost your backlink profile.
 List your business in local directories: Websites like Yelp or even your local chamber of
commerce directory allow businesses to include their website links when registering. These
backlinks not only help local SEO but also increase your visibility.
Also, don’t miss out on community events. Participating in or sponsoring local events often gets your
business mentioned on local websites, blogs, or news outlets. These mentions usually come with
backlinks, which helps your SEO.
Finally, keep your Google My Business profile updated with your website link. It increases the chance of
your business showing up in local search results and helps you connect with other local businesses,
which can lead to more backlinks from community sites and blogs.
7). Monitor Your Backlink Profile
Keep an eye on your backlinks is very important. If you don’t know who’s linking to your site, you might
miss out on issues that can hurt your ranking.
One of the SEO tips to remember is not all backlinks are good for you. Some can actually bring your site
down.
To make sure your backlinks are helping you, you can use tools like SEMrush. This tool will show you
who’s linking to your site and how good those links are. It can help you spot any bad or spammy links
that might be dragging you down.
If you find bad backlinks, don’t worry—you can disavow them. This means telling search engines to
ignore those bad links.
Here’s how you can do it:
 Identify the bad links: Use your monitoring tool to find links from spammy or low-quality sites.
 Create a disavow file: List all the bad links you want to disavow.
 Submit to Google: Go to Google’s Disavow Tool and upload your file.
By monitoring your backlink profile regularly, you can catch problems early and keep your site healthy.
Remember, it’s easier to fix issues before they become big problems.
8). Avoid Bad Backlink Practices
When it comes to backlinks, not all strategies are good for your SEO.
Bad practices like link farming, buying backlinks, or using excessive reciprocal links can harm your site big
time. If you want long-term success, focus on ethical strategies.
 Link farming is when a group of websites all link to each other just to manipulate search
rankings. It might seem like a quick win, but search engines can catch onto it fast, and you can
end up with a penalty.

 Buying backlinks is another risky move. It may seem tempting, but buying links from low-quality
sites will hurt your SEO in the long run. Search engines are strict about this, and it can cause your
rankings to drop.
 Excessive reciprocal links (where two sites link back and forth) can also raise red flags. While
some back-and-forth linking is fine, overdoing it can make search engines think you’re trying to
game the system.
Instead, focus on ethical backlink-building strategies:
 Create content that others want to link to.
 Reach out to relevant sites with personalized pitches.
 Guest blog or collaborate with industry peers.
The key is to play the long game—focus on quality, not quantity, and you’ll see steady, sustainable
results.
Conclusion
We’ve covered some of the SEO tips to remember when building quality backlinks.
From creating content that people want to link, to building real relationships in your niche and
monitoring your backlink profile—it’s all about doing it right.
Remember, it’s better to have a few good links than tons of bad ones.
Focusing on quality over quantity will set your website up for long-term success. It might take a bit more
effort, but the results are worth it.
So take the time to build those strong backlinks, and you'll see your site grow and thrive over time.

Another important widget is the shopping cart widget. This lets customers put items in their cart and

examples:

 Live Chat: This lets customers ask questions right away, so you can help them fast.

Using the right ecommerce widgets can really change how you run your ecommerce business. They help

Once you install ecommerce widgets, they help manage everything from your product catalog to online

items are the hottest sellers, like a specific pair of shoes.
It can also let you know how many visitors check out your site daily, helping you understand trends and
plan your inventory better.
c). Inventory Management
An inventory management widget notifies you when stock is low. If your best-selling jacket is almost out,
you’ll get a reminder to reorder it before customers start asking for it.
d). Simplify Checkout Processes
A shopping cart widget makes it easy for customers to add items and complete their purchases. When
customers can check out quickly, they are more likely to return to shop again.
e). Customer Feedback
A review widget lets customers leave feedback on their purchases. When new shoppers see glowing
reviews about a must-have item, it builds trust and can convince them to make a purchase.
These widgets work well with ecommerce platforms like Shopify and WooCommerce. They’re easy to
add and can really help your online business grow.
My Top 8 Ecommerce Widgets for Website Owners
I’ve put together my top 10 ecommerce widgets that can make running your website easier and help
increase your sales as it did for me.
These tools are simple to use and can really change how your store operates.
Let’s take a closer look!
1). Yotpo ($79 - $169/month)

Yotpo is a powerful tool for collecting and displaying customer reviews and ratings on your ecommerce
site.
This ecommerce widget for website is designed to enhance the customer experience by showcasing real
feedback from shoppers. When potential buyers see positive reviews, it builds trust and motivates them
to buy.
Let’s say you’re browsing an online store and see a product with great reviews. You’re more likely to buy
it, right?
Yotpo’s review widget can prominently display these ratings on the product page, making it easy for
customers to see what others think.
This not only helps in increasing conversions but also keeps your customers engaged with your brand.
For example, if you own an online electronics store, displaying reviews from satisfied customers who

Knowing that previous buyers had a positive experience can lead to more sales. With Yotpo, you can turn

 Photo Reviews: Allows customers to upload photos along with their reviews, adding visual
credibility.
 Social Sharing: Facilitates easy sharing of reviews on social media, increasing brand visibility.
 Ratings Display: Prominently features product ratings to influence new customers.
 Analytics Dashboard: Provides insights into review performance and customer engagement
metrics.
 Q&A Widget: This feature lets customers ask questions about products. Other customers or the
store owner can answer, helping to provide additional information and reassurance before a
purchase.
This combination of features makes Yotpo a must-have tool for any online business looking to enhance
trust and drive sales.

2). Shopify ($24 - $2,300/month)

Shopify is a top ecommerce platform that makes it easy to set up your own online store. It comes with

With its user-friendly design and helpful features, Shopify is great for both beginners and experienced

Whether you want tools for sending newsletters or for tracking your inventory, there's an app for you.

4). Ecwid Widget Suite ($0 - $89/month)

Whether you have a blog, a small business site, or even a social media page, the Ecwid Widget Suite

Imagine running a local bakery with a simple website. With Ecwid, you can showcase your delicious cakes

What makes Ecwid stand out is how easy it is to use.
You don’t need to be a tech expert to set it up. Just add the widgets to your site, and you’re ready to go!
Plus, it integrates well with popular platforms, so you can manage everything from one place.

 Secure Payments: Ecwid supports various payment methods so you can meet the needs of

 Mobile-Friendly Design: The store works well on mobile devices, making sure it looks nice and
works properly for customers shopping on their phones.
 Multi-Language Support: With this feature, you can reach customers around the world. It makes

With these features, the Ecwid Widget Suite is a powerful set of ecommerce widgets that can help you
create a professional-looking product catalog on any website builder.
It’s a great way to increase your online sales and connect with more customers!
5). WebEngage(Available on Request)

WebEngage is a great tool that helps businesses connect better with their customers through
personalized messages.
This platform is perfect for any ecommerce business that wants to improve how they engage with their
customers.
You can send messages to your customers centered on their actions on your website. That’s what
WebEngage allows you to do!
With WebEngage, you can create special messages that make customers feel appreciated. For example, if
someone leaves items in their shopping cart, you can send them a quick reminder.
This kind of message helps encourage them to complete their purchase.
The platform uses customer data to understand what your shoppers want. If a customer looks at a
specific product but doesn’t buy it, WebEngage can send them an email with a discount or related offers.
This helps keep your brand in their minds and makes them more likely to come back.
Its major features are:

 Push Notifications: WebEngage sends real-time alerts and messages to users. For example, if a

 Email Marketing: This feature automates email campaigns based on how users behave. If a

 User Segmentation: You can target specific groups of users for tailored marketing strategies. For

feel valued.
 Feedback Collection: WebEngage helps you gather insights from customers about their
experiences through feeback forms. This feedback is vital for improving your services and
products.
 Behavior Tracking: It monitors user interactions on your site. By understanding what customers
like or dislike, you can refine your marketing efforts and improve overall customer data.
With these features, WebEngage makes it easier for ecommerce platforms to build strong relationships
with customers and drive sales.
6). Linnworks (£349/month)

Linnworks is a tool that helps online retailers manage their inventory and orders easily. If you sell

It keeps everything organized, so you don’t have to stress about keeping track of stock or orders.
Imagine running an ecommerce store where you sell on sites like eBay, Amazon, and your own website.
Linnworks allows you to see all your sales in one place. This means you won’t accidentally sell something

Linnworks also makes order management simple. Instead of typing in each order by hand, the platform

Its major features are:
 Inventory Synchronization: Keeps stock levels the same across different platforms.
 Order Management: Makes processing orders faster and easier.
 Reporting Tools: Shows how well your sales are doing and the health of your inventory.
 Integration Capabilities: Connects with many ecommerce tools and platforms.
 Multi-Channel Support: Lets you sell on several platforms at once.
With these features, Linnworks is an essential tool for any ecommerce store looking to enhance their

7). TrustPulse ($5-$39/month)

TrustPulse is a tool that helps online businesses show real-time customer activity on their websites.
It’s designed to build trust and encourage more sales by displaying notifications of recent purchases or
sign-ups.
For instance, if you sell handmade jewelry online. With TrustPulse, when someone buys a beautiful

This not only catches the attention of other visitors but also encourages them to consider buying too, as

One great feature of TrustPulse is its Real-Time Notifications. These alerts show visitors that people are
actively buying, which can create a sense of urgency.
You can also customize how these notifications look to match your brand so they blend nicely into your

Its major features are:
 Real-Time Notifications: Shows alerts about recent purchases or sign-ups to encourage other
visitors.
 Customizable Display Options: Adjusts how notifications appear to fit your brand.
 Increased Urgency: Helps create a feeling that customers should buy quickly.
 Analytics Dashboard: Tracks the effectiveness of your notifications.
 Integrations: Works well with popular ecommerce platforms to enhance functionality.
With these features, TrustPulse is a valuable tool for any online business looking to improve the

8). Privy ($24-$45/month)

Privy is a tool that helps online businesses capture email addresses and increase sales. It focuses on

With Privy, you can create a pop-up that offers a discount to visitors who sign up for your email list. This

understand what resonates with your customers.
Its major features are:
