 Landing Pages: Dedicated pages for promotions and email sign-ups.
 Exit-Intent Offers: Targets users as they attempt to leave the site.
 A/B Testing: Allows testing of different forms to see which performs better.
 Analytics: Gives you insights into how your campaigns are performing.
With these features, Privy is a useful tool for any online business that wants to increase customer
engagement and increase sales.
Essential Ecommerce Widgets Every Website Needs
We’ve already covered my top 8 ecommerce widgets for website owners. Now, let’s focus on a few
essential ones that are a must for your website.
These ecommerce widgets are must-haves for any online business. While there are many other widgets,
these essentials make shopping easier, increase sales, and keep customers happy.
Here's a list of important ecommerce widgets every website should use:
a). Shopping Cart Widget
Shopping cart widgets are a must-have for any ecommerce website. It lets customers easily view, add,
and change their purchases.
It should support easy online payments and work with payment options such as PayPal or credit cards.
b). Product Catalog Widget
A clear product catalog helps customers find what they want quickly. This widget organizes your products
so shoppers can easily browse. For instance, if you sell clothes, having filters for size and color can help
customers find their favorites.
c). Customer Review Widget
Trust is important when shopping online, and a customer review widget builds that trust. By showing
real customer feedback, visitors can see what others think about your products. Positive reviews help
new buyers feel more confident about their choices.

d). Inventory Management Widget
Keeping track of your stock is important for any ecommerce store. An inventory management widget
helps you monitor your products in real time, so you always know what’s available and can avoid
overselling.
e). Payment Gateway Widget
This widget makes it easy and safe for customers to make online payments. Choose a payment gateway
that works with multiple currencies and offers secure transactions. This helps reduce the chances of
customers abandoning their carts.
f). Social Media Integration Widget
Social media can help promote your products. This widget lets customers share their favorite items on
platforms like Facebook and Instagram, bringing more traffic to your online business.
g). Loyalty Program Widget
A loyalty program widget rewards your regular customers. By offering points for purchases or discounts
for repeat visits, you encourage them to keep coming back. This builds a loyal customer base.
h). Email Capture Widget
Collecting email addresses is important for staying connected with customers. An email capture widget
helps you gather emails by offering discounts or special deals. This builds your email list and keeps
customers updated.
i). Live Chat Widget
A live chat widget allows customers to ask questions while they shop. This immediate support can
improve customer satisfaction and often leads to more sales.
j). Abandoned Cart Recovery Widget
This widget sends reminders to customers who leave items in their carts. A gentle nudge, like an email
with a discount, can encourage them to finish their purchase.
k). Exit-Intent Popup Widget
This widget offers deals when visitors are about to leave your site, helping capture those who might
abandon their shopping session.
l). Shipping Calculator Widget
A shipping calculator shows costs before checkout, helping customers know what to expect and reducing
surprises during the purchase process.
m). Analytics Widget
An analytics widget tracks user behavior and sales performance, giving you insights to make smart
decisions about your products and marketing.

n). Referral Program Widget
This widget encourages customers to refer friends and family, offering rewards for successful referrals to
help grow your customer base.
o). SEO Tools Widget
This widget helps optimize your product pages for search engines, improving your site’s visibility and
attracting more traffic.
p). Wishlist Widget
A wishlist widget lets customers save items for later. This keeps them engaged and encourages them to
return to your store.
q). Product Recommendation Widget
This widget suggests products based on what customers have browsed. By showing them related items,
you can increase the chances of more purchases.
r). Video Embed Widget
This widget allows you to add product videos to your pages. Showcasing items in action can improve
engagement and help customers make choices.
s). Feedback Collection Widget
This widget collects feedback and opinions from customers, helping you know their needs and improve
your services.
t). Event Calendar Widget
An event calendar shows upcoming sales or promotions, keeping customers informed about special
offers.
With these essential ecommerce widgets, you can create a better shopping experience for your
customers and drive more sales.
How Do You Set Up Ecommerce Widgets on Your Website?
I’m going to show you a step-by-step process to add ecommerce widgets to your website.
These widgets can greatly improve how your online store works and make the shopping experience
better for your customers.
Let’s take a quick look at this process.
1. Choose Your Ecommerce Platform
First, decide which ecommerce platform you’ll be using.
For this guide, I’ll focus on Shopify, but if you’re using platforms like WooCommerce or Wix, don’t worry!
The steps are quite similar.

Each of these platforms has its own features, but they all make adding widgets straightforward.
Tip: The key is to pick widgets that integrate directly with your platform to avoid compatibility issues.
2. Select the Right Widgets
Once you've chosen your platform, the next step is selecting the widgets that will best improve your
store’s functionality. Think about which ones you need for your store. Some common widgets include:
 Shopping Cart Widget: This helps customers manage their purchases.
 Customer Review Widget: Builds trust by showing feedback from real buyers.
 Payment Gateway Widget: Ensures secure online payments.
When I logged into my Shopify account, I went to the search bar at the top of the page. I typed in
"shopping cart widgets" to find a specific widget that meets my needs.

When I typed in the shopping cart widgets, I was directed to the Shopify App Store, where I browsed
through the available options for widgets built for Shopify.


After looking at the ratings and reviews, I selected the Qikify Slide Cart widget. It’s a great choice
because it’s free and integrates perfectly with Shopify.
Once you find the right widget, read through its details and features to make sure it meets your needs.
The Qikify Slide Cart widget, for example, adds a "sticky" cart that follows users as they shop, making it
easier for them to check out.
3). Install the Widgets
Now that you’ve selected your widget, it’s time to install it. Here’s how to do it for Shopify,
WooCommerce, and Wix:
Shopify Installation Steps:
 Click on the widget you want, in this case, "qikify Slide Cart,” and then click “Add app.”
 Follow the steps to install the widget in your store.


After clicking "Install," Shopify will ask for permission to access your store's data, such as viewing orders
and managing products.
After installing the widget, you will be guided step by step on what to do to set up the widget on your
Shopify store, as seen in the image below.

WooCommerce Installation Steps:
 From your WordPress Dashboard, click on Plugins.
 Select Add New and search for the widget you need.
 Once you find the right plugin, click Install and then Activate it.
Wix Installation Steps:
 Log into your Wix account and open your site’s editor.

 Go to the App Market and search for your widget, like "shopping cart widget."
 Click the Add to Site button and follow the instructions to finish the installation.
4). Customize the Widgets
Once installed, you need to customize the widget so it matches the look and feel of your store.
Customizing the widget ensures it integrates smoothly with your store’s theme and functionality. For
example, with the qikify Slide Cart widget, you can adjust the cart's colors, placement, and style.

In the customization screen, you’ll be able to adjust settings like visibility on desktop and mobile, as well
as features like cart upsells, discount codes, and shipping goals.
5). Test the Widgets
After customizing, it’s essential to test the widget to make sure it works as expected. Here’s how you can
do this:
 Shopping Cart Widget: Add items to your cart and check if they appear correctly.
 Customer Review Widget: Leave a test review and see how it displays on your product page.
 Payment Gateway Widget: Complete a test checkout to verify that the payment process is
seamless.
This step is important because you want to ensure that your widgets are functional and that customers
can use them without any issues.
6). Monitor and Optimize
After everything is set up and working, it’s important to monitor your widgets to see how they are
performing.
Most platforms like Shopify and WooCommerce offer analytics tools that let you track how customers
are interacting with your widgets.

For example, if the customer review widget isn’t getting much interaction, you may want to move it to a
more visible spot on the product page.
By following these steps, you can easily set up ecommerce widgets on your website.
What to Consider Before Adding Widgets to Your Ecommerce Website
Adding widgets to your e commerce website can make your store more functional and engaging, but you
need to keep a few things in mind before adding them.
Here’s what you should consider:
a). Website Speed
Installing too many ecommerce widgets can slow down your website. This impacts the overall website
functionality and can frustrate customers.
To avoid this, only choose the necessary widgets. For example, a shopping cart widget is essential, but
you don’t need to overload your site with unnecessary features. Stick to the essentials to keep your
online store running as it should.
b). Mobile-Friendly
Most shoppers today use mobile devices to browse ecommerce websites, so make sure that the widgets
you add are mobile-friendly. A widget that doesn’t adjust to mobile screens could ruin your customer’s
experience.
For instance, if your product catalog or customer review widget looks out of place on a mobile screen,
customers might leave without making a purchase. Always ensure that your ecommerce platform
supports responsive widgets that work well on all devices.
c). User Experience
Take into consideration how each widget will affect the user experience. Widgets should improve
navigation and shopping, not make it harder.
A well-placed review widget or payment gateway widget can enhance trust and convenience, while too
many pop-ups can annoy customers. Focus on widgets that will add value, like those that help with
publishing product-related content or simplifying checkout.
By being mindful of these factors, you’ll ensure that your ecommerce site not only looks good but works
well for customers.
Keep an eye on multiple data reports to track how your widgets are performing, and adjust them if
needed to optimize your online store.
Common Issues With Ecommerce Widgets (And How to Solve Them)
Ecommerce widgets can make your online store better, but sometimes they come with problems.
Here are some common issues you might face and how to fix them.

a). Slow Website Speed
 Problem: Adding too many widgets can slow down your website. When your site is slow,
customers might leave before making a purchase.
 Solution: Choose only the essential widgets. Regularly check your site’s speed using tools like
Google PageSpeed Insights. Remove any widgets that aren’t necessary.
b). Mobile Compatibility Issues
 Problem: Some widgets don’t work well on mobile devices. If they look weird or don’t function
properly, mobile shoppers may get frustrated.
 Solution: Always check if the widgets you choose are mobile-friendly. Test them on different
devices to ensure they look good and work well.
c). Poor User Experience
 Problem: Widgets that are hard to use or confusing can annoy customers. If a widget interrupts
their shopping experience, it could lead to abandoned carts.
 Solution: Select simple widgets and enhance the shopping process. Make sure your layout is
clean and easy to use.
d). Incompatibility with Other Tools
 Problem: Sometimes, widgets can clash with other plugins or tools, causing errors.
 Solution: Before installing a new widget, check if it’s compatible with your existing ones. Read
reviews to see if others faced similar issues.
e). Widgets Not Displaying Properly
 Problem: Widgets might not show up on your site due to coding issues or incorrect installation.
 Solution: Double-check the installation instructions. If something isn’t working, reach out to the
widget’s customer support for help.
f). Lack of Customization Options
 Problem: Some widgets don’t allow much customization, which can make them look out of place
on your site.
 Solution: Choose widgets that offer customization options. This way, you can adjust the colors,
fonts, and layouts to fit your brand.
g). Not Enough Analytics
 Problem: If a widget doesn’t provide analytics, you won’t know how it’s performing.
 Solution: Look for widgets that include reporting features. This way, you can track how well
they’re working and make necessary adjustments.
h). Security Concerns
 Problem: Adding widgets can sometimes create security risks, especially if they handle sensitive
customer information.

 Solution: Always choose reputable widgets from trusted developers. Check reviews and ensure
they comply with security standards.
i). Difficulty in Updating Widgets
 Problem: Some widgets may require frequent updates, which can be a hassle.
 Solution: Opt for widgets that update automatically or require minimal intervention. Keep track
of updates to avoid any issues.
j). Inconsistent Branding
 Problem: Widgets that don’t match your store’s style can confuse customers.
 Solution: Look for widgets that allow branding customization. Make sure they align with your
website’s colors and fonts for a cohesive look.
Ready to Get Started?
We've talked about a lot of important widgets that can help your online store. From Yotpo, which helps
gather customer reviews, to Shopify’s tools that make managing your shop easy, these widgets can really
help your website.
They make it easier for your customers to browse and buy, and they can keep them coming back.
By carefully selecting and installing the right ecommerce widgets, you're setting your business up for
success.
Now, it’s time to get started!
Check out these widgets and start making the kind of sales you have always wanted.
FAQ: Ecommerce Widgets for Your Website
1. How do widgets work on ecommerce websites?
Widgets operate as small applications that integrate with your ecommerce platform to perform specific
functions, such as displaying product reviews, enabling social media sharing, or managing shopping
carts. They enhance user interaction and overall site functionality.
2. Can I put a website as a widget?
Yes, you can embed websites as widgets on your site. This allows you to display content from other sites,
like social media feeds or external product catalogs.
3. How do I create a widget?
Creating a widget typically requires programming knowledge, but many platforms offer ready-made
widgets that you can customize. If you want to build one from scratch, you might need to hire a
developer or use widget creation tools available in your ecommerce platform.
4. How do I add a widget to my website?

To add a widget, you can typically follow these steps: find the widget in your platform’s app store, click to
install it, and then customize its settings to fit your website’s design and functionality.
5. What does a widget look like on a website?
Widgets can come in different forms, like buttons, forms, or small interactive elements. They should
blend seamlessly with your website’s design and be easy for users to interact with.
6. How can I create a shortcut widget for my website?
Shortcut widgets can often be created through your website’s builder or app store. Look for options that
allow you to add buttons or links to key pages or features on your site.
7. Can widgets be added to any type of website?
Most widgets are designed to be compatible with popular ecommerce platforms like Shopify,
WooCommerce, and Wix. However, always check the widget’s compatibility with your specific website
type before installation.
8. How do I turn a link into a widget?
You can create a widget from a link by using HTML code to embed it on your site. This requires some
coding knowledge, or you can use a widget generator tool to make it easier.
9. Can you add ecommerce to an existing site?
Yes, you can add ecommerce to an existing website. You can use plugins, widgets, or services like Ecwid
or Shopify to add ecommerce features without starting a new site. If you need more advanced options,
consider hiring a developer for custom solutions.
10. What’s the difference between a widget and a web part?
A widget is a small application that offers specific functionality on a website, like a weather display or a
shopping cart. In contrast, a web part is a component of a web page that shows content and features,
often part of larger systems like SharePoint. The main difference is that widgets are standalone tools,
while web parts are integrated into broader frameworks.

This feature makes my content more accessible to a global audience, enhancing the learning experience
for my students.
I’ve received feedback from international students who appreciated the added accessibility.
e). AI Lesson Writing Assistant

Writer’s block can be a significant obstacle when creating course content. Teachable’s AI Lesson Writing
Assistant helps overcome this by providing content suggestions and structure.
This tool, integrated into the text block, has made it easier for me to draft lessons and refine them,
making the content creation process much more efficient.

Feature #2: Easy and Flexible Payments

Managing payments and ensuring an easy transaction process is crucial for any online business.
Teachable’s payment features have simplified this aspect for me, allowing me to focus more on creating
and less on administrative tasks.
a). Hassle-Free Payment Options
Teachable’s flexible payment options have been a game-changer.
With Teachable, I can let my students pay using PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, debit and credit cards,
and even Buy Now Pay Later options.
This flexibility has made it easier for students to enroll and has significantly boosted my sales. I noticed a
20% increase in enrollment after offering these diverse payment options.
b). Get Paid When You Want
Teachable understands the diverse financial needs of course creators, which is why they offer flexible
payout schedules.
Whether I need daily, weekly, or monthly payouts, Teachable has me covered. This feature helps me
manage my cash flow and plan my business expenses well.
For instance, choosing weekly payouts helped me better align my marketing spending with incoming
revenue.
c). Tax Worries? Not Here
Dealing with taxes used to be a headache, but not anymore.

Teachable calculates, collects, and remits sales taxes on my behalf, simplifying the process and saving me
from additional accounting work.
This feature has been a huge relief and allows me to focus on what I love – creating and selling courses.
Feature #3: Increasing Sales and Marketing Efforts
Marketing and sales tools are vital for reaching more students and increasing revenue.
Teachable provides an array of features that have made my marketing efforts more effective and
streamlined.
a). Subscription Success
One of my favorite features is the subscription pricing model.
This allows students to access my content as long as they continue to pay their fees, providing me with a
steady stream of recurring revenue. It’s a win-win situation – students get continuous learning, and I get
reliable income.
Implementing this model led to a 30% increase in my monthly revenue, as many students preferred the
ongoing learning option.
b). Bundling for Value

Teachable makes it easy to bundle courses, adding more value for students and increasing my sales.
Creating attractive packages that appeal to my audience has helped increase my earnings and provided
comprehensive learning experiences.
c). Lead Magnets Magic
Building an audience is essential, and Teachable’s lead magnet feature helps with that.
By giving away free content in exchange for contact details, I can gather leads and expand my email list.
This strategy has been key to expanding my reach and setting up successful marketing campaigns.

d). Order Bumps and Upsells

Teachable allows me to offer additional products or services during checkout, known as order bumps.
This feature significantly increases my average order value by suggesting related courses or resources.
Upsells are also very easy, letting students make additional purchases with a single click after they’ve
bought a course.

e). Coupons and Promotions

Creating a sense of urgency and increasing transaction value can be achieved with coupons.
Teachable allows you to generate and manage coupons easily, providing incentives for students to
purchase your courses. This feature has proven effective in boosting my sales during promotions.
During my last Black Friday sale, the use of coupons doubled my usual monthly sales.
Feature #4: Creating a Thriving Community
Being part of a supportive community and having access to educational resources can significantly
impact your success.
Teachable offers several features that foster a strong creator community and provide ongoing support.

a). Learning from the Best with Teachable

Teachable offers a library of mini-courses packed with strategies to build and grow an online business.
These courses have helped me learn a lot and use smart techniques in my own business.
It's really important for creators to take courses from other creators too. When you learn from others,
you get new ideas and tips. This keeps you updated with what's working well.
You can see what successful creators do and try those things yourself. Learning from others can make
you better and help your business grow even more.
b). Supportive Creator Community at Teachable
Being part of Teachable has connected me with over 10,000 creators. This community has been fantastic
for networking, trading ideas, and getting support.
It’s like having a team of cheerleaders who understand the challenges and victories of online course
creation. The feedback and tips I received helped me improve my course content significantly.
c). Product Webinars for Deep Dives
Teachable’s product webinars offer in-depth guides to new features and sneak peeks at what’s coming
next.
These webinars have provided valuable insights and helped me make the most of the platform’s
capabilities.
d). Launch Accelerator Challenge

Although I haven’t had a chance to use Teachable's Launch Accelerator Challenge, yet, I have heard many
great things.
Launched just last year, this program has been a game-changer for many creators. It guides users
through the process of getting their courses up and running in just 30 days.
The expert advice and structured approach have been incredibly helpful for others, allowing them to
launch ahead of schedule and see immediate enrollments.
It’s definitely something I’m considering for my next course!
e). Teachable for Every Sale
Teachable celebrates every sale I make, offering greater access and benefits as I move up the ranks.
This feature has been a great motivator and has added an extra layer of excitement to my sales
achievements.
The rewards program encouraged me to reach higher sales targets, which I did consistently.
f). Live Chat for Quick Help
When I have questions, live chat support is available to help.
Available for Pro, Pro+, and Business plans, this feature provides fast answers to pressing questions,
ensuring I can resolve issues quickly and keep my business running without any problems.

Feature #5: Detailed Analytics & Reporting

Knowing how students engage with my courses and tracking financial performance is important for the
continuous improvement of my business.
Teachable’s analytics and reporting tools provide the insights I need.
a). Insightful Course Reports
Teachable’s course reports provide stats on lecture and video completion, quiz scores, and course
leaderboards. This data helps me gauge student engagement and identify areas for improvement.
By analyzing these reports, I made adjustments that led to higher completion rates and better student
feedback.
b). Comprehensive Sales Reports
Teachable’s sales reports allow me to monitor total sales, earnings, refunds, chargebacks, affiliate
commissions, and payouts. These reports give me a clear picture of my business’s financial health.
c). Student Progress Tracking
Knowing how my students progress through my courses helps me support them better.
Teachable’s student progress reports provide data on lesson completion, video viewing, and quiz scores,
helping me identify where students might need additional support.
By focusing on these areas, I was able to offer targeted help and improve overall course satisfaction.

d). Easy Integrations
Teachable integrates with apps like Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, and Hotjar. These tools
show me how students use my courses and school.
With this information, I can make data-driven choices to make the learning experience even better.
Feature #6: Advanced Tools for Experienced Creators
For those looking to take their course creation to the next level, Teachable offers advanced tools that
provide greater control and customization.
a). Effortless Integrations
Teachable’s integrations, including Zapier, allow me to connect with the tools I already use and love. This
makes my work easier and helps my business run smoothly.
b). Powerful Public API
For more advanced needs, Teachable’s public API lets me automate managing students and products,
create detailed reports, and connect with other tools. This helps me run my online business more
efficiently.
c). Customizing My Theme
Advanced theme customizations enable me to ensure my school and products are 100% on-brand. With
code snippets and custom CSS, I can remove Teachable branding and create a truly unique site.
d). Tailored User Roles
Managing a team is easier with Teachable’s custom user roles. I can control what users can and can’t do
in my school, ensuring collaborators have the access they need without compromising sensitive
information.
e). Bulk Student Imports
Adding students one by one can be tedious. With Teachable’s bulk student import feature, available on
the Business plan, I can save time by importing students in bulk, making course management much more
efficient.
Whether you’re just starting out or looking to scale your online school, Teachable offers the tools and
support you need to succeed.
The Good and Bad Sides of Using Teachable
Alright, let’s get real about Teachable. It’s been a big part of my journey in creating and selling online
courses.
But like anything, it’s got its highs and lows.
Here’s my take on the good and bad sides of using Teachable based on my own experience and what
others have shared.

The Good
1). User-Friendly Interface
Teachable is really easy to use. You don’t need to be a tech expert. The drag-and-drop builder makes
creating your course pages simple and fun.
When I started, it was like playing with digital Legos! No stress about coding or anything like that.
2). Course Completion Certificates
Everyone loves a little recognition. Teachable make it easy to create and give out course completion
certificates.
My students love getting these certificates. It’s a great way to motivate them and give them something
to show for their hard work.
3). Easy for Students
Teachable isn’t just easy for me; it’s also super user-friendly for my students. They can easily find their
way through courses, quizzes, and materials.
I’ve had so much positive feedback about how straightforward the platform is to use.
4). Reliable Hosting
Imagine your videos buffering in the middle of a lesson. Nightmare, right?
Thankfully, Teachable offers reliable hosting with high-quality playback on various devices. My students
can watch videos smoothly without any interruptions, keeping them engaged and happy.
5). Community Building Features
Building a community around your courses can really enhance the learning experience.
Teachable’s features, like discussion forums, comment sections, and live Q&A sessions, have helped me
create a sense of community among my students. This has not only improved engagement but also
made learning more interactive and fun.
6). Regular Updates and Improvements
Teachable is always getting better. They often release updates and new features to make the user
experience better. Every update feels like an upgrade to my business tools.
Other pros include AI-powered tools for easy course creation, great customer service, increased sales
and marketing efforts, thriving community support, detailed analytics and reporting, and many more.
The Bad
1). Limited Customization Options
While Teachable does offer customization, it can be somewhat limited. For instance, fully customizing
email templates and landing pages to match your brand isn’t as extensive as I’d like.
This can make it tough to maintain a consistent brand experience across all touchpoints.

2). Transaction Fees
Teachable charges transaction fees on all sales, which can add up over time. Depending on the plan,
these fees can range from 5% to 0%.
While this might not seem like much initially, it can significantly impact your profits, especially if you’re
selling a lot of courses.
3). Downtime and Maintenance
Like any large platform, Teachable experiences occasional downtime for maintenance.
While these times are typically scheduled during off-peak hours, they can still be inconvenient if you
have a global audience.
I’ve had instances where students in different time zones couldn’t access their courses, which was
frustrating.
4). Limited Course Types
Teachable is primarily designed for video-based courses.
While you can add other types of content, like quizzes and surveys, the platform doesn’t support as
many different types of educational content as some other platforms. This can be a limitation if you want
to offer a more diverse range of learning materials.
5). Limited Reporting
The reporting tools on Teachable, while useful, are somewhat limited. For instance, you can’t track the
performance of individual emails or landing pages in great detail.
This makes it harder to analyze and optimize your marketing campaigns. However, integrating Teachable
with third-party analytics tools like Google Analytics can help mitigate this issue.
Overall, despite its few cons, I’ve found Teachable to be a valuable tool in my journey as a course creator.
Its strengths far outweigh the weaknesses, and it has helped me grow my online business.

What the Different Plans Cost

Let’s talk about Teachable plans and pricing. If you’re thinking about setting up your own online school,
it’s super important to know what each plan costs and what you get.
I’ve been through it all, so let me break it down for you in a way that’s easy to understand.

1). Free Plan
Cost: $0/month
What You Get:
• 1 Published Product: Whether it’s a course, coaching service, or digital download, you can
launch one product.
• No-Code Course Builder: Create your course website and landing page without any coding skills.
• Student Referrals: Encourage your students to refer others to your courses.
• Teachable:pay: Integrated payment processing is used to handle transactions.
• Admin & Author Seat: You can manage everything yourself or with one additional person.
Personal Take: The Free Plan is a fantastic starting point if you’re just starting with online courses.
However, keep in mind that there’s a $1 + 10% transaction fee on paid courses. It’s great for testing the
waters, but you might quickly outgrow it if your courses gain traction.
2). Basic Plan
Cost: $59/month
What You Get:
• 5% Transaction Fee: Lower than the free plan but still something to consider.
• 5 Published Products: Launch more courses, coaching services, or digital products.
• Community: Build a community around your courses.
• Integrated Email Marketing: Engage with your students directly through Teachable’s email
system.
• Coupons and Order Bumps: Offer discounts and additional products during checkout to increase
sales.
• Custom Domains: Use your own domain name to brand your online school.
• Live Group Coaching and Accelerator Challenge Access: Extra resources to help you grow.
Personal Take: The Basic Plan is where you start to get serious. I upgraded to this plan when I had a few
courses ready to go. The lower transaction fee and additional products were a big plus. The email
marketing tool also helped me keep in touch with my students and drive more sales.
3). Pro Plan
Cost: $159/month
What You Get:
• 0% Transaction Fees: No transaction fees, which means more money in your pocket.
• 50 Published Products: Plenty of room to grow your course library.
• Unlimited Membership Tiers: Create different membership levels for your students.
• Affiliate Marketing: Leverage others to promote your courses for a commission.
• Live Chat Support: Get quick help when you need it.
• Upsells to Increase Order Value: Offer additional products or services during checkout.

• Public API Access: This is for those who need more customization.
• Removable Branding: Make your site look more professional by removing Teachable’s branding.
• 5 Admin & Author Seats: Great for small teams.
Personal Take: The Pro Plan is a solid choice if you’re serious about scaling your online school. I loved the
zero transaction fees and the ability to launch up to 50 products. Live chat support was a lifesaver more
than once when I ran into technical issues.
4). Pro+ Plan
Cost: $249/month
What You Get:
• Everything in the Pro Plan, plus:
• 200 Courses, Coaching Products, and Digital Downloads: A huge library capacity for diverse
offerings.
• Custom User Roles: Manage your team with tailored access levels.
• 200 Product Bundles: Package multiple products together to offer more value.
Personal Take: The Pro+ Plan is for those who are really looking to expand and need a lot of room for
growth. The custom user roles are particularly useful if you have a larger team and need to control who
can access what.
4). Business Plan
Cost: $665/month (Billed Annually)
What You Get:
• Unlimited Courses, Coaching Products, and Digital Downloads: No limits on what you can offer.
• Unlimited Admin & Author Seats: Perfect for larger teams.
• Advanced Theme Customizations: Get full control over the look and feel of your site.
• Bulk Student Enrollment: Efficiently manage large enrollments.
• Custom User Roles: Further manage team access and responsibilities.
Personal Take: The Business Plan is the big league. If you’re running a large operation with a significant
number of courses and a big team, this plan makes sense. The advanced customizations and bulk
enrollments are key features for scaling up your operations.
So, there you have it – a breakdown of Teachable pricing. Each plan offers different features tailored to
varying needs.
Whether you’re just starting with a single course or looking to scale a large online school, Teachable has
a plan that can fit your needs.
Remember, it’s all about finding the right balance between cost and features that works for you.

How to Set Up Your First Online Course on Teachable
When I set up my first course on Teachable, I followed these exact steps. I remember how exciting it was
to see my course live and to get the first few enrollments.
Using Teachable’s built-in email marketing, I was able to reach out to potential students and increase my
course sales significantly.
Setting up your first online course on Teachable might seem a bit overwhelming at first, but trust me, it’s
pretty straightforward once you get the hang of it.
I created another account on the free plan to show you how to get through each stage.
Let’s walk through the steps together so you can get your course up and running in no time.
Step 1: Create Your Teachable Account
First things first, you need to sign up for a Teachable account.
Head over to Teachable and sign up. You can start with the free plan, which is perfect for beginners. Just
fill in your details, and you’re good to go!


Step 2: Set Up Your School
Once you’ve logged in, it’s time to set up your online school. This will be the home for all your Teachable
courses.
Create a New School: Click on the “Create a new school” button.
Name Your School: Choose a name that represents your brand or the topic you’re teaching.
Add Branding: Upload your logo and customize the colors to match your branding.


Step 3: Create Your First Course
Now, let’s create your first course.
Go to Courses: In your admin dashboard, click on the “Courses” tab.
Add a New Course: Click the “New Course” button.
Enter Course Details: Fill in the course title and description as shown below. Make it catchy and
informative to attract students.

Add a Thumbnail Image: Upload a thumbnail image for your course. This image will be displayed at
checkout and throughout the member experience. You can upload one now or choose one later.


Set a Price: Choose a pricing model for your course. Options include one-time purchase, payment plan,
subscription, and free. Set the price that reflects the value of your course.


Outline Your Course: Decide whether to generate your course outline with AI or start from scratch. This
outline will help you structure your course curriculum well.

Step 4: Build Your Curriculum
This is where the fun begins. You’ll start adding your course content.
Create Sections and Lectures:
• Click on “Curriculum” in the course editor.
• Click “New Section” to add a section (like a module).
• Click “Add New Lecture” to add lectures (individual lessons) within each section.


Upload Content:
• Video: Upload your course videos (recommended format is MP4).
• Text: Add written content directly or upload documents.
• Quizzes: Add quizzes to engage your students and test their knowledge.
• PDFs: Upload supplementary PDFs.


Organize Your Content: Drag and drop your lectures to organize them in the desired order.
Step 5: Customize Your Course Pages
You want your course to look professional and engaging. Here’s how you can do it:


Edit the Sales Page: Click on “Sales Pages” in the left-hand menu. Customize your sales page with
compelling text, images, and a promo video to attract and inform potential students. Make sure to
highlight the benefits of your course and include a clear call to action.

Set Up the Checkout Page: Ensure the checkout process is smooth and easy to follow. Personalize the
checkout page to fit your brand. You can add additional fields to collect necessary information from your
students.

Customize the Thank You Page: After students purchase your course, they should be directed to a thank
you page or the course curriculum. This page can include a thank you message, instructions on how to
access the course, and any additional information they might need.

Default Post Purchase Page: Specify where a student should be taken after buying this course. Typically,
this would be the Thank You Page.
Step 6: Set Your Pricing
Teachable offers several pricing options to fit your needs and the needs of your students. Here’s how to
set it up:

Go to Pricing: In the course editor, click on the “Pricing” tab.

• Choose a Pricing Model: You have four main options to choose from:
• Free: Allow access to your content free of charge. This is great for lead magnets or introductory
courses.
• One-time Purchase: Set a one-time payment for lifetime access to your course.
• Payment Plan: Offer a fixed number of monthly payments. This makes higher-priced courses
more accessible.
• Subscription: Set up recurring payments. This is ideal for ongoing access to content, such as
memberships or continuous education.
Set the Price: Enter the price that you want to charge for your course. Make sure it reflects the value of
the content you’re offering. Consider your audience’s budget and compare it with competitors’ pricing.
Here are some examples of pricing models:

• Free: Great for introductory lessons or lead magnets.
• One-time Purchase: $99 for full access to "How to Avoid Common SEO Mistakes in Content
Writing."
• Payment Plan: $35/month for 3 months for access to the course.
• Subscription: $20/month for ongoing access to SEO content and updates.
Setting the right price is a balance between covering your costs, compensating your time and effort, and
being accessible to your target audience.
Once you’ve decided on the pricing model and amount, click “Save” to apply these settings.

Step 7: Publish Your Course

You've put in all the hard work creating your course, and now it's time to make it available to your
students.
Publishing your course on Teachable is the final step to getting your content out there.
Preview Your Course: Before you publish, it's a good idea to preview your course to ensure everything
looks perfect. Click the "Preview" button at the top right of your curriculum page to see your course, as
your students will see it.
Publish Each Section and Lecture: Go through each section and lecture in your course curriculum and
click the "Publish" button next to them. This makes each piece of content available to your students.
Final Review: Double-check that all your content is correctly uploaded, organized, and published. Ensure
that any quizzes, PDFs, and videos are functioning properly. Verify that your course description,
thumbnail, and pricing are set up the way you want.
Publish Your Course: Once you’re confident everything is in place, click the "Publish" button for your
entire course. This will make your course live and available for enrollment.
Step 8: Promote Your Course
Now that your course is live, it’s time to attract students. Here’s how to get the word out:

Use Social Media: Share your course on platforms like Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Instagram. Create
posts that show why your course is valuable and include a direct link.
Email Marketing: Send out different emails to your subscribers to tell them about your new course.
Share exciting details about what they'll learn and why they should join.
SEO: Improve your course pages for search engines to get more visitors. Use keywords in your course
title, description, and content to boost your search engine ranking.
Limited-Time Discounts: Offer a temporary discount or special bonus to encourage early sign-ups.
Gather Testimonials: Encourage your first group of students to provide testimonials and reviews. Positive
feedback can be incredibly powerful in attracting new students.
Step 9: Engage with Your Students
Interaction is key to a successful online course. Engaging with your students keeps them motivated and
enhances their learning experience.
Enable Comments: Allow students to leave comments on lectures. This encourages interaction and
provides a platform for students to ask questions and share insights.
Live Q&A: Host live sessions to answer questions and engage with students in real time. This can be
done through webinars or live chats.
Track Progress: Use Teachable’s analytics to monitor student progress. Identify areas where students
may be struggling and make necessary improvements to your course content.
Setting up your first online course on this learning management system might feel a bit overwhelming at
first, but don’t worry—it’s easier than you think.
Just follow these steps, and you’ll have your course up and running in no time.
Teachable Showdown: Comparing Top Learning Platforms
Making and selling online courses is a great way to share what you know and make money.
I’ve used Teachable, Udemy, Kajabi, and Thinkific, and I’m here to share my experiences to help you pick
the best one.
1). Teachable vs. Udemy
Teachable:
• Ownership and Control: Teachable lets you have full control over your content, pricing, and
student data. You can customize your course pages and brand them to match your style.
• Revenue Model: Teachable’s professional and business plans allow you to keep most of your
earnings minus a small transaction fee on lower-tier plans.
• Course Creation Tools: The drag-and-drop builder is super user-friendly. I could easily upload
videos, create quizzes, and add PDFs without hassle.

Udemy:
• Marketplace Model: Udemy brings a large audience to your courses, but you have less control
over pricing and promotions because Udemy runs frequent sales.
• Revenue Sharing: Udemy takes a significant cut from your sales. It’s great for exposure but not
so much for making much profit.
• Course Creation Tools: Udemy’s tools are straightforward but less customizable compared to
Teachable. They’re designed to get you started quickly but can feel limiting if you want more
control over your course content.
Personal Insight: If you want more control and higher revenue share, Teachable is the way to go. If
you’re looking for easy exposure with less effort on marketing, Udemy can be beneficial.
2). Teachable vs. Kajabi
Teachable:
• Flexibility: Teachable offers flexibility with different pricing models, including one-time
payments, subscriptions, and payment plans. This helped me tailor my pricing strategy to
different audience segments.
• Ease of Use: It’s straightforward and perfect for focusing on content creation without being
bogged down by complex settings.
• Professional and Business Plans: These plans offer advanced features like affiliate marketing and
detailed analytics, which are fantastic for scaling your business.
Kajabi:
• All-in-One Solution: Kajabi is an all-in-one platform. It’s like having a course builder, email
marketing tool, and website builder all in one place. This was fantastic for scaling my business.
• Advanced Marketing Tools: Kajabi’s marketing features are top-notch. Automated email
sequences, sales funnels, and detailed analytics helped me streamline my marketing efforts.
• Higher Cost: The downside? It’s pricey. Kajabi’s cost can be a barrier if you’re just starting out. I
found it worth the investment as my business grew, but it’s a big upfront commitment.
Personal Insight: If you’re looking for an integrated solution and have the budget, Kajabi’s advanced
features can take your business to the next level. For simpler, cost-effective course creation, Teachable is
a solid choice.
3). Teachable vs. Thinkific
Teachable:
• Transaction Fees: Teachable’s free and basic plans come with transaction fees, which are
eliminated in the higher-tier plans.
• Course Builder: The course builder is easy to use, but it doesn't offer all the advanced
customization options that Thinkific offers.
Thinkific:
• No Transaction Fees: Thinkific doesn’t charge transaction fees, even on their free plan. This was
a huge plus when I was starting out.

• Course Builder: Thinkific’s course builder is highly intuitive and allows more advanced design
options. The drag-and-drop functionality is similar to Teachable but with more flexibility.
• Customization and Community: Thinkific offers better tools for community building, including
forums and discussion features. This was great for engaging students beyond the course content.
Personal Insight: Thinkific’s no transaction fees and advanced customization make it attractive,
especially if you want to build a community around your course. Teachable’s simplicity and ease of use
make it a great starting point.
From my experience:
• Teachable is great if you want to have control over your course content and pricing without
needing to learn too much tech stuff.
• Udemy is perfect for quickly getting your course in front of a big audience, but you'll have to give
up a chunk of your earnings.
• Kajabi is awesome if you want everything in one place, including advanced marketing tools, but
be ready to spend more upfront.
• Thinkific is fantastic for those who want lots of customization and community-building features
without having to pay transaction fees. It’s perfect for growing your brand.
Pick the platform that fits what you need and want. Each one has its own strengths, so knowing what
they offer can help you make the right choice.
So, is Teachable worth it?
Absolutely, yes!
Teachable is a fantastic choice for launching online courses. It's user-friendly, packed with powerful
features, and offers excellent support.
Whether you're just starting or have been teaching online for a while, Teachable has something for you.
I’ve found it incredibly easy to customize and manage my courses on Teachable. The minimal transaction
fees on higher plans mean I get to keep more of my earnings.
Teachable's drag-and-drop course builder makes it easy to create professional courses without any tech
headaches.
Flexible payment options like PayPal and Apple Pay make it simple for students to pay, increasing your
sales.
The platform's AI tools save you time and enhance course creation. Marketing tools help you reach a
wider audience and grow your revenue.
You'll also benefit from a supportive creator community and detailed analytics to track progress and
performance.
If you're ready to create and sell courses without stress, Teachable is definitely worth trying.
Sign up for Teachable today and start your journey to success!

Title: Inspiring Women in History Every Girl Should Know

Primary Keywords: Inspiring women, women in history, Nigerian women leaders, female pioneers

Short Description: Discover inspiring women in history who changed the world and inspire every girl to dream big.

Inspiring Women in History Every Girl Should Know

"From Nigeria to the world, meet women in history who broke limits, challenged norms, and inspire girls to dream boldly and act fearlessly."

Women have shaped the world in powerful yet often under-recognized ways for centuries. From science labs and courtrooms to protest grounds and Olympic stadiums, women have challenged societal expectations, broken through barriers, and changed history.

Their stories aren't just historical records; they're beacons of courage, intellect, and resilience for girls everywhere.

Learning about these women isn't just about knowing the past. It's about teaching girls today that greatness isn't defined by gender, background, or geography.

When young girls see women who look like them doing extraordinary things, they believe they can do it too.

Here are some of the most inspiring women in history, trailblazers whose stories every girl should know.

Trailblazers in Science and Education

1). Marie Curie (Poland/France, 1867–1934)

Marie Curie's story is one of relentless curiosity and groundbreaking achievement. In a time when women were discouraged from pursuing science, she not only entered the field but changed it forever.

She became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize in Physics (1903, shared with her husband, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel), and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, earning a second in Chemistry (1911).

Her research into radioactivity led to significant advances in cancer treatment and nuclear energy.

2). Dr. Wangari Maathai (Kenya, 1940–2011)

Wangari Maathai was the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, but her impact extends far beyond the award.

She founded the Green Belt Movement, which mobilized thousands of women in Kenya to plant millions of trees and restore degraded land.

She championed environmental conservation, women's empowerment, and political freedom, often at significant personal risk. Her work laid the foundation for global conversations on sustainability and women's leadership in environmental action.

3). Dr. Stella Adadevoh (Nigeria, 1956–2014)

Dr. Stella Adadevoh's courage in the face of crisis saved Nigeria from what could have been a devastating Ebola outbreak.

In 2014, she correctly diagnosed the first case of Ebola in Lagos and made the life-saving decision to quarantine the patient, despite facing immense pressure to release him. Her actions prevented the virus from spreading across Nigeria's densely populated urban areas.

Today, the Dr. Ameyo Stella Adadevoh Foundation upholds her legacy by promoting public health, research, and policy.

4). Ada Lovelace (United Kingdom, 1815–1852)

Ada Lovelace is known as the world's first computer programmer, even though she lived in the 1800s, long before modern computers were invented. She worked with Charles Babbage, a mathematician who designed one of the first mechanical computers.

Ada wrote notes explaining how this machine could follow instructions to do calculations, what we now call code. Her ideas helped lay the foundation for modern computer science.

Icons of Political Change and Civil Rights

5). Rosa Parks (USA, 1913–2005)

Often referred to as the "mother of the civil rights movement," Rosa Parks is best known for refusing to give up her seat to a white man on a segregated bus in Alabama in 1955.

That act of civil disobedience launched the Montgomery Bus Boycott, which lasted over a year and became a significant turning point in the U.S. civil rights struggle.

Parks was not just a tired seamstress—she was a lifelong activist and community organizer whose quiet strength spoke volumes.

6). Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti (Nigeria, 1900–1978)

Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti was a political powerhouse and one of the earliest Nigerian women to fight colonial oppression and advocate for women's rights.

She organized thousands of market women to protest unfair taxation and poor working conditions under British rule. She founded the Abeokuta Women's Union, one of Nigeria's most formidable women's movements.

Her contributions laid the groundwork for feminist activism in West Africa and inspired future generations of women leaders.

7). Malala Yousafzai (Pakistan, 1997–present)

At just 15 years old, Malala Yousafzai was shot by the Taliban for advocating girls' education in northern Pakistan.

She survived the attack and continued her mission on the global stage, becoming the youngest person to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

Through the Malala Fund, she fights for every girl's right to education, especially in regions where girls are most at risk of being left behind. Her voice remains a powerful force for justice and access to education worldwide.

8). Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria, 1954–present)

A respected economist and global leader, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala made history as the first African and first woman to lead the World Trade Organization (WTO).

Before that, she served twice as Nigeria's Finance Minister and once as Foreign Minister, the first woman to hold both roles. Known for her fight against corruption and her efforts to stabilize Nigeria's economy, she also spent 25 years at the World Bank, rising to Managing Director.

Her leadership is widely recognized worldwide, and she advocates for trade equity, global health, and women's empowerment.

9). Margaret Thatcher (United Kingdom, 1925–2013)

Margaret Thatcher was the first woman to become Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. She led the country from 1979 to 1990, making her the longest-serving British leader of the 1900s.

Known as the "Iron Lady," she was strong and determined. She significantly changed the UK's economy by reducing government control and encouraging private business.

Many people admired her for her leadership, while others disagreed with her ideas. Still, she remains one of the most important leaders in modern history.

Artists, Writers, and Cultural Icons

10). Frida Kahlo (Mexico, 1907–1954)

Frida Kahlo turned personal pain into provocative and unforgettable art. After a bus accident left her with lifelong injuries, she began painting vivid self-portraits that explored identity, gender, politics, and her own physical suffering.

Her unique style, combining realism and fantasy, has made her one of the most influential artists of the 20th century. The Frida Kahlo Museum in Mexico City celebrates her life, work, and unapologetic authenticity.

11). Maya Angelou (USA, 1928–2014)

Poet, singer, civil rights activist, and memoirist, Maya Angelou used the power of words to speak out against racism, sexism, and injustice. Her autobiography, I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, brought the Black female experience to the forefront of American literature.

Angelou, a celebrated performer and speaker, advised world leaders and received numerous honors. Her legacy is preserved through her official site, which features her writings and speeches.

12). Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie (Nigeria, 1977–present)

Chimamanda is one of the most celebrated contemporary writers to emerge from Nigeria. Her novels, including Half of a Yellow Sun and Americanah, tackle themes of identity, feminism, post-colonialism, and migration.

Her TED Talk, We Should All Be Feminists, sparked global conversations about gender roles and has been translated into multiple languages. She's a leading voice in reshaping how African stories are told globally.

Athletes Who Broke Barriers

13). Chioma Ajunwa (Nigeria, 1970–present)

Chioma Ajunwa made history in 1996 as the first Nigerian and African woman to win an Olympic gold medal in a field event. Her long jump at the Atlanta Olympics was not just a win for her, but for an entire nation.

Ajunwa's triumph came after years of struggling with injury, setbacks, and a lack of institutional support. Today, she is a vocal advocate for clean sports and youth development.

14). Serena Williams (USA, 1981–present)

With 23 Grand Slam singles titles to her name, Serena Williams is a tennis legend and a cultural icon. She's known for her unmatched power, resilience, and competitive spirit. Off the court, she has advocated for equal pay, maternal health, and racial justice.

Her official WTA profile tracks her victories, but her influence goes far beyond sports; she's inspired women everywhere to play hard, dream big, and speak up.

15). Alice Coachman (USA, 1923–2014)

In 1948, Alice Coachman became the first Black woman to win Olympic gold, dominating the high jump in London. Her achievement broke racial and gender barriers at a time when segregation was still legal in the U.S.

After the Olympics, she became a role model for young athletes and continued to advocate for youth sports programs.

You can read more about her journey and legacy through the Team USA archives.

Conclusion

From different times and places, these women broke barriers and changed the world in powerful ways.

Their stories remind every girl that anything is possible with courage, hard work, and vision. Learning about them is not just inspiring, it's a reminder that greatness begins with believing in yourself.

Researched by Victoria Odueso

title: How to Excel in Email Marketing for Cleaning Service
content:
How to Excel in Email Marketing for Cleaning Service
“Want to grow your cleaning service? Check out these easy, practical email marketing for cleaning
service tips that can help you connect with your clients”.
Running a cleaning business is no walk in the park.
Between managing your team, keeping clients happy, and making sure every job is spotless, there's
always something demanding your attention.
And let’s face it, making your business stand out and keeping customers loyal can be a real challenge.
But what if I told you there's a simple, cost-effective way to connect with your customers and grow your
business?
Email marketing for cleaning service businesses is your answer.
It’s a powerful tool that can help you build strong relationships and keep your cleaning services at the
forefront of your clients' minds.
Today, I'm going to share some tips on how you can use email marketing to make your cleaning business
bigger.
Trust me, what I am about to tell you is going to be the game changer for your business.
Here’s what we’ll talk about:
 Getting Started with Email Marketing: Easy steps to kick things off.
 Choosing the Right Email Software: Finding the best tools for you.
 Writing Emails That Work: Tips to create messages your customers will love.
By the end of this post, you’ll know how to set up an email marketing campaign that helps your cleaning
services company stand out and keep your customers coming back.
Let’s get started!
Why Email Marketing for Cleaning Service is a Game Changer
With email marketing, you have a direct line with your customers. It is also cheap, effective, and helps
build relationships.
Whether you're a small cleaning company or a professional cleaning company offering commercial
cleaning services, this direct communication can make all the difference.
This is what you stand to gain from email marketing :
 Stay in Touch: Think of email marketing as a way to keep in touch with your clients.
 Offer Deals: Use it to offer special deals and promotions.
 Customer Reminders: Remind people why they love your service.


As you can see, email marketing can truly elevate your business as a cleaning business owner. If you
haven’t started yet, now is the perfect time.
Who Are the People You Want to Reach?
Now the next step is figuring out who exactly you want to reach. Let’s identify and connect with your
ideal clients.
Find Your Ideal Clients
Who are your ideal clients?
Think about homeowners who need regular cleaning or businesses looking for reliable commercial
cleaning services.
Most cleaning businesses focus on a mix of residential and commercial clients to get more customers
and make more money.
Create Buyer Personas
Let’s create profiles of your ideal clients to make your marketing efforts more effective:
 Define Key Characteristics: age, location, job title, and cleaning needs.
 For Instance: One persona could be "Busy Professionals" who need regular cleaning services to
save time, while another could be "Small Business Owners" looking for reliable, affordable
cleaning for their offices.
 Tailor Your Emails: Use these personas to ensure you're speaking to the right person with the
right message.
When you know who you’re reaching out to, you can create more effective email templates that
resonate with your audience.
It might take more effort, but connecting with your ideal clients will lead to more successful campaigns
and, ultimately, more deals.
From Zero to Thousands: Building Your Email List
Every big email list starts small. Imagine turning a few contacts into thousands of loyal customers.
With the right steps, you can grow your email list quickly and easily.
Here's how to get started.
a). Starting from Scratch
No email list? No problem! Start by asking your existing clients for their emails.
When you complete a job, simply ask if they’d like to receive updates and special offers from your
cleaning services company.

b). Using Existing Contacts
Your current clients are gold. Get their permission to send updates.
Reach out to them through your social media account or in-person interactions to let them know about
the benefits of staying connected.
c). Lead Magnets
Offer something in return for an email address. A simple cleaning checklist or a discount can work
wonders.
For instance, a commercial cleaning company could offer a free guide on maintaining office cleanliness
between professional deep cleanings.
Cleaning businesses can provide exclusive discounts on top-notch cleaning services for those who sign
up.
By following these steps, you will, in no time, build an email list that helps you market your cleaning
services just as you desire.
How to Make Your Emails the Most Opened in the Inbox
You know how sometimes you get tons of emails and just ignore most of them?
I don’t want that happening to your emails. Here’s how to make sure your emails get noticed and
opened.
1). Catchy Subject Line
First things first, the subject line. This is the first thing people see. Make it interesting and to the point.
Think along the lines of "Save Time with These Cleaning Hacks" or "Get Your Home Sparkling Clean in
No Time." Make it sound like there’s something useful inside.
A great subject line can decide if people open or ignore your email.
Example:
 Bad: “Newsletter - Week 3”
 Good: “3 Easy Ways to Keep Your Home Sparkling Clean!”
2). Keep It Short
People are busy.
They don’t have time to read long emails. Keep your message short and sweet. Get straight to the point.
Tell them what they need to know without extra fluff.
Example:

 Bad: “In this week’s newsletter, we have a lot of exciting things to share with you. We’ve included
updates on our services, some great tips for keeping your home clean, and a special offer for our
loyal customers. We hope you enjoy it!”
 Good: “Check out our top cleaning tips and a special offer just for you!”
3). Be Personal
When people see their name, they feel special. It’s like the email is just for them.
Also, talk to them like you would talk to a friend. Mention the recipient's past interactions or
preferences.
Example:
 Bad: “Dear Customer, we have a new offer for you.”
 Good: “Hi Jane, we know you loved our last deep cleaning service, so here’s a special offer just
for you.”
4). Add a Little Mystery
Sometimes, a bit of mystery can make people curious. This makes them want to open the email to find
out more.
Example:
 Bad: “Our new cleaning products are available now.”
 Good: “You Won’t Believe What We’re Offering This Month!”
5). Use a Recognizable Sender Name
Make sure your name or your company’s name is clear in the “From” field. If they know you, they’re
more likely to open your email.
Example:
 Bad: “info@cleaningcompany.com”
 Good: “Gladys from Sparkle Clean Services”
6). Email Design
Keep it clean and professional. You don’t need to be fancy, just clear and engaging.
Use simple layouts that are easy to read and look good on both desktop and mobile.
Include clear calls to action so your readers know exactly what to do next, whether it's booking a service
or clicking for more information.
Example:
 Bad: An email with very small text and big images that don’t fit the screen.
 Good: A clean, simple layout with readable text and images that adjust to the screen size.

7). Offer Value
Give them something they want. It could be tips, discounts, or useful info. Make them feel like opening
your email is worth their time.
Example:
 Bad: “We’re having a sale.”
 Good: “Get 20% Off Your Next Cleaning Service - Just for You!”
8). Ask Questions
Sometimes, asking a question can make people interested.
Example:
 Bad: “Our latest cleaning services are available now.”
 Good: “Need Help With Your Cleaning? Check Out Our New Services!”
9). Include a Call to Action
Tell your readers what you want them to do next.
Example:
 Bad: “We have some new services.”
 Good: “Book your cleaning now and get 20% off!”
10). Test What Works
Try different things and see what works best. Maybe one subject line gets more opens than another.
Example:
 Test A: “5 Tips for a Cleaner Home”
 Test B: “How to Make Cleaning Easier for You”
So there you have it!
Try these tips to make your emails more noticeable and get more people to open them. See which ones
work best for you!
4 Winning Email Templates for Your Cleaning Service in 2024
Email marketing is a very useful marketing strategy for cleaning business owners. But figuring out what
to say can feel overwhelming.
Don’t worry, I’ve got you covered.
Here are five email templates that will help you connect with potential customers and grow your
professional cleaning company.

Template 1: The Friendly Introduction
Subject: Get to Know [Your Cleaning Service] – Professional Cleaning for Your Home
Hi [Customer Name],
I hope you’re doing great!
I’m [Your Name] from [Your Cleaning Service]. We specialize in making homes sparkle with our top-notch
deep cleaning services. Our team is all about giving you the best cleaning experience possible.
Here’s a bit of what we offer:
 General cleaning: Regular upkeep to keep your home tidy and fresh.
 Deep cleaning: Thorough cleaning that tackles every nook and cranny.
 Move-in/move-out cleaning: Perfect for making your new or old home spotless.
Our professional cleaning team uses eco-friendly products to ensure a safe environment for you and
your family.
Plus, we’re fully insured, so you can have peace of mind knowing your home is in good hands.
Got questions or want to book a cleaning? Just reply to this email or give us a call at [Your Phone
Number]. We’re here to help!
Best regards,
[Your Name]
[Your Position]
[Your Cleaning Service]
Why it works: This template is all about being warm and approachable. It introduces your cleaning
services effectively and lets potential clients know how to get in touch with you. Plus, it sets the tone for
future communication.
Template 2: The Helpful Hand
Subject: Need Help Keeping Your Home Clean? We’re Here for You!
Hi [Customer Name],
We know keeping a home clean can be tough, and we’re here to make it easier for you.
At [Your Cleaning Service], we handle everything from regular cleaning to deep cleaning services. Let us
take care of the dirty work so you can enjoy your clean home.
Here’s what we can do for you:
 Regular cleaning: Weekly or bi-weekly visits to maintain your home’s cleanliness.
 Deep cleaning: Comprehensive cleaning that includes hard-to-reach areas.
 Specialized cleaning: Services like window cleaning, carpet cleaning, and more.

Our team is trained to handle all types of cleaning tasks efficiently. We understand that every home is
unique, so we easily tailor our services to meet your specific needs.
Want to know more? Just reply or call us at [Your Phone Number]. We’d love to chat!
Best,
[Your Name]
[Your Position]
[Your Cleaning Service]
Why it works: This email shows you understand the challenges your customers face and offers a
straightforward solution. It’s empathetic and easy to respond to, making it appealing to potential
customers.
Template 3: The Success Stories
Subject: See How We’ve Helped Families Like Yours!
Hi [Customer Name],
We’re proud to have helped many families keep their homes clean and cozy. Here’s what one of our
happy customers had to say:
“[Customer Testimonial]”
We’d love to help you too! Interested in our services? Just reply to this email or give us a call at [Your
Phone Number].
To give you an idea, here are a few examples of how we’ve made a difference:
 Family A: With three kids and two pets, Family A struggled to keep their home clean. Our regular
cleaning services helped them maintain a tidy and safe environment for their children.
 Family B: Moving out of a rental property, Family B needed a thorough cleaning to get their
deposit back. Our move-out cleaning service left the place spotless, and they received their full
deposit.
 Family C: Elderly couple who found it hard to keep up with house chores. Our team provided
deep cleaning services that made their home comfortable and hygienic.
We’d love to help you achieve the same results. Just reply to this email or give us a call at [Your Phone
Number].
Best,
[Your Name]
[Your Position]
[Your Cleaning Service]

Why it works: Sharing real stories from satisfied customers builds trust and shows potential clients that
you deliver on your promises. This kind of social proof is crucial for convincing new clients to try your
services.
Template 4: The Special Offer
Subject: Special Offer Just for You – 20% Off Your First Cleaning!
Hi [Customer Name],
We have a special treat for you! Get 20% off your first cleaning with [Your Cleaning Service].
Whether you need a one-time deep clean or regular services, we’re ready to help. Here’s what you can
expect:
 One-time deep clean: Perfect for spring cleaning or prepping for a special event.
 Regular services: Weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly cleaning to keep your home consistently clean.
 Custom packages: We can create a cleaning plan that fits your needs and schedule.
Our team uses the best cleaning products and techniques to ensure your home is spotless. Plus, we’re
flexible with scheduling to accommodate your busy life.
Reply to this email or call us at [Your Phone Number] to book your appointment. Don’t miss out on this
exclusive offer!
Can’t wait to hear from you,
[Your Name]
[Your Position]
[Your Cleaning Service]
Why it works: Everyone loves a good deal. This email grabs attention with a special offer and encourages
potential clients to take the next step. It's an excellent way to generate leads and attract potential
customers.
Using these email templates, you can easily tailor your messages to connect with your target audience,
generate leads, and build a loyal customer base for your cleaning business.
Just personalize these templates to fit your style, and watch your email campaigns bring in more leads
and satisfied customers!
With the right email marketing software, you can manage your email campaigns and track their
effectiveness, ensuring your marketing strategies are always on point.
When and How Often to Send Your Emails
Getting the timing and frequency of your email campaigns right is super important for marketing your
cleaning services. Here’s how to nail it:

1). Best Times to Send Emails
 When’s the best time to send emails? Early mornings and evenings tend to work best.
 Why? People are more likely to check their inboxes during these times, increasing your chances
of being seen.
2). Finding the Right Frequency
 Don’t overwhelm your clients. Start with once a week and see how it goes.
 Why this works: This keeps your cleaning services in mind without being annoying.
 Adjust based on feedback: Some clients might prefer bi-weekly updates, while others might be
happy with monthly newsletters.
Satisfied customers are more likely to share your services with others, creating word-of-mouth buzz that
attracts more leads.
For example, a cleaning service I know started sending their sales emails early in the morning and saw an
immediate increase in responses.
They also included clear calls to action and shared testimonials from happy customers. This made their
emails feel more personal and engaging.
Remember, it’s not just about sending more emails but about sending the right emails. So, experiment a
little, see what works best, and adjust your strategy as needed.
How to Automate Your Emails
Automating your emails saves you time and ensures your clients get the attention they deserve. Here’s
how to get started:
a). Email Marketing Tools
Use tools like Mailchimp and Constant Contact, these platforms have easy-to-use templates and
automation features that help you send the right message at the right time, leading to more conversions.
b). Setting Up Automation
 Automate new client emails: Set up a welcome email that goes out automatically when a new
client signs up. This introduces your services and sets expectations.
 Follow-up emails for old customers: Schedule follow-up emails to check in and offer special
deals, ensuring they feel valued and appreciated.
Automating your cold emails saves you time and helps you reach new clients easily. This way, you can
focus on other parts of your business while your email marketing works for you.
Track Your Success: Make Your Emails Better
Keeping track of your email marketing helps you see what's working and where you can improve. Here’s
how:

a). Key Metrics to Track
 Open rates and click rates: High open rates mean your subject lines work. High click rates mean
your content is engaging.
b). Making Adjustments
 Change based on feedback: If emails aren’t doing well, tweak subject lines or content.
 Experiment: Try different approaches to see what grabs attention and leads to more
conversions.
c). Feedback Loop
 Ask for feedback: Use surveys to learn what clients like or dislike.
 Adjust based on feedback: Make changes to meet client preferences, like adding more tips or
special offers.
By tracking your metrics, making adjustments, and keeping a feedback loop, you can improve your email
marketing and get better results for your cleaning service.
Pro Tip: Keep Your Content Fresh and Exciting
Keeping your email content up-to-date is important to keep your audience interested and engaged.
Here’s how you can go about that:
a). Regular Updates
 Stay current: Share the latest tips and promotions.
 Monthly refresh: Highlight new cleaning tips or recent success stories.
b). Seasonal and Special Promotions
 Holiday deals: Offer special discounts during holidays.
 Example: A New Year’s discount on deep cleaning services.
c). Stay Relevant
 Trendy topics: Include current trends in cleaning and email marketing.
 Expert insights: Talk about popular new cleaning products or methods.
When you keep your content fresh, you can rest assured that your emails will remain interesting and
useful to your audience.
Are You Ready to Put in The Work?
Email marketing is a powerful tool that can help you connect with clients, grow your business, and keep
your cleaning services top of mind.
By following the tips and templates I've shared, you can create engaging emails that your customers will
love.

Timing is key, so send your emails when people are most likely to see them. Focus on sending
meaningful emails that offer value.
Automate where you can to save time and keep things consistent. Regularly update your content to
keep your audience interested.
Mix in helpful tips, success stories, and special offers to keep your emails engaging. Track your success,
make necessary adjustments, and stay connected with your clients.
Don’t wait any longer!
Start putting these strategies to work today and watch your email marketing efforts pay off.
