title: Why Drinking Water Does More for Your Skin Than You Think
content:
Title:
Why Drinking Water Does More for Your Skin Than You Think

Keywords:
Hydration for skin health, benefits of drinking water for clear skin, water and skin elasticity, how hydration affects eczema and psoriasis, daily water intake for better skin

Short Description:
Drinking enough water helps your skin stay clear, smooth, and healthy. This article examines the actual impact of hydration on skin texture, tone, and common skin conditions.

Why Drinking Water Does More for Your Skin Than You Think

"Find out how proper hydration helps reduce dryness, dullness, and signs of aging naturally."

"Drink more water, it's good for your skin!"

We've all heard this skincare mantra repeated by dermatologists, beauty influencers, and health coaches alike.

But how often do we stop to ask why? What's really happening beneath the surface when we sip that glass of water?

While it may seem like simple advice, staying hydrated does more than just quench your thirst; it affects everything from your skin's texture to how well it fights off breakouts and signs of aging.

If you are still not convinced, in this article, we'll break down exactly how water supports healthy, glowing skin, and why it might be the most underrated step in your skincare routine.

Keep reading to find out more!

How Water Affects Your Skin

With around 64% of your skin made up of water, hydration isn't just helpful, it's the foundation of how your skin looks, feels, and functions. When you're dehydrated, your skin loses elasticity, becomes dry, and starts to look dull.

Water helps maintain:

  • A strong skin barrier that keeps out irritants and locks in moisture
  • Elasticity, which prevents sagging and fine lines
  • A smooth, even texture, making skin appear healthier

Research shows that increasing your water intake can significantly improve skin hydration and overall appearance, especially if you're usually dehydrated.

So, when people say, "Drink more water for better skin," they're not wrong; your skin relies on it to stay healthy from within.

Why Drinking Water Does What Moisturizers Can't

Moisturizers are great for locking in hydration, but they only work on the outer layer of your skin.

Drinking water, on the other hand, hydrates your skin from the inside, reaching all layers and supporting long-term skin health.

When you're well-hydrated:

  • Your skin cells function better, improving tone, texture, and elasticity
  • There's less risk of dryness and flaking, even before applying products
  • Your skin responds better to your skincare routine overall

While topical products treat the surface, internal hydration supports deeper skin layers that products can't reach.

That dewy look you're chasing with serums? It starts with your water bottle.

Hydrated Skin = More Elastic, Less Wrinkled Skin

Skin elasticity is what keeps your face looking firm and youthful. When you're dehydrated, your skin loses that bounce, making fine lines and sagging more noticeable.

Water helps maintain the skin's structure by supporting collagen production and keeping skin cells plump. The result? Skin that stretches and snaps back easily instead of creasing and folding.

If you're relying only on creams to fight wrinkles, you're missing a key piece.

Bottom line: water won't erase wrinkles overnight, but it supports the kind of skin structure that keeps them from forming in the first place.

Does Drinking Water Help Your Skin Detox?

While your liver and kidneys are the primary detoxifiers, staying hydrated supports their function and can indirectly benefit your skin.

  • Supports Natural Detoxification: Adequate water intake helps the kidneys and liver flush toxins, reducing the burden on the skin to eliminate waste.
  • Reduces Skin Issues: Dehydration can lead to dryness, tightness, and flakiness, making the skin more prone to irritation and breakouts.
  • Improves Skin Clarity: By facilitating the removal of waste products, proper hydration can contribute to a clearer, more radiant complexion.

Hydration and Acne: What's the Connection?

You've probably heard that drinking more water can help prevent acne, but how true is that?

While water alone won't clear up your skin overnight, it plays an important supporting role in preventing and managing breakouts.

Here's how:

  • Reduces oil buildup: When your skin is dehydrated, it produces more oil to compensate, which can lead to clogged pores and breakouts. Staying hydrated helps maintain balanced oil levels.
  • Flushes out toxins: Water helps your body eliminate waste. The fewer toxins your body needs to expel through the skin, the lower your risk of flare-ups.
  • Improves healing: Hydrated skin recovers faster. If you experience inflamed or irritated breakouts, drinking water can help support the healing process.
  • Reduces inflammation: Dehydration can increase skin inflammation, making acne look worse. Hydration helps calm the skin from the inside out.

Water isn't a cure for acne, but it helps create the conditions your skin needs to stay balanced, clear, and less reactive.

What About Hydration and Chronic Skin Conditions?

Proper hydration can help manage chronic skin conditions like eczema and psoriasis.

  • Eczema: Dehydrated skin worsens eczema by increasing dryness and irritation. Drinking enough water helps maintain the skin's moisture barrier, reducing flare-ups and itchiness.
  • Psoriasis: While hydration alone won't cure psoriasis, it supports skin cell health and can ease scaling and discomfort when combined with treatments.

How Much Water Do You Really Need for Healthy Skin?

You've probably heard the classic "8 glasses a day" advice, but that's outdated and doesn't reflect your actual hydration needs.

The Actual Recommendation

According to the U.S. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, the daily fluid intake (from all sources: water, beverages, and food) should be:

  • About 15.5 cups (3.7 liters) for men
  • About 11.5 cups (2.7 liters) for women

This includes water from beverages (such as tea, coffee, and juice) and from foods (such as fruits, soups, and vegetables).

What About the "Half Your Body Weight in Ounces" Rule?

You might've heard this quick formula:

Drink half your body weight in ounces. For example, if you weigh 150 lbs, drink 75 oz (~2.2 liters) of water per day.

  • This is a useful estimate, especially for people trying to be mindful of hydration.
  • However, it's not a scientifically proven fact, and it doesn't account for other factors, such as exercise, diet, or environment.

It's best used as a starting point, not a rigid rule.

Factors That Affect How Much Water You Need

  • Climate: Hot or dry weather makes you sweat more, increasing your fluid needs.
  • Activity level: If you exercise regularly, you lose water through sweat and need to replenish it.
  • Diet: High-sodium, low-fiber, or high-protein diets require more water to process. On the other hand, eating water-rich foods like cucumbers, oranges, or watermelon can help with hydration.
  • Caffeine and alcohol: These are natural diuretics and can increase fluid loss, meaning you may need to drink extra water to compensate.

Signs You're Getting Enough Water

When your skin is properly hydrated, you'll likely notice:

  • A dewy or natural glow (even without makeup)
  • Less dryness, flaking, or rough patches
  • Improved skin elasticity, your skin bounces back when pinched
  • A more even skin tone and texture
  • Fewer breakouts and faster healing

Signs You Might Be Dehydrated

  • Dull, tight, or itchy skin
  • Dark circles or puffiness around the eyes
  • More pronounced fine lines or creases
  • Cracked lips or dry patches
  • Fatigue and sluggishness (your body and skin slow down)

Tips for Staying Hydrated

  • Start your day with a glass of water, and your body wakes up slightly dehydrated.
  • Carry a refillable water bottle so you're never caught without it.
  • Add natural flavors (such as lemon, cucumber, or mint) if plain water bores you.
  • Use a hydration reminder app or set alarms to sip throughout the day.
  • Don't wait until you're thirsty; thirst is a late sign of dehydration.

Final Thoughts

Drinking water does far more for your skin than simply quenching thirst.

While it's not a miracle cure, consistent hydration lays the foundation for healthier, clearer, and more radiant skin.

I challenge you to swap one soda or juice for water today; your skin will absolutely love you for it.

Researched by Victoria Odueso

content:
How To Recover Deleted Videos from Instagram Video
Downloader
“Accidentally deleted your Instagram videos? Learn how to recover deleted videos from Instagram
video downloader with these easy steps and restore your content.”
We’ve all experienced the frustration of losing an Instagram video or photo.
You may accidentally delete an important post or suddenly notice that your Instagram photos are
disappearing.
Sometimes, Instagram reel drafts or videos planned for upload vanish due to things like virus attacks or
formatting errors on your device.
So, can you restore lost or deleted Instagram photos, videos, stories, IGTV videos, or reels? Thankfully,
yes, there are several ways to do it!
In this guide, I’ll show you the different methods to recover your deleted Instagram content, whether
you’re using an Android or an iPhone.
From checking the recently deleted folder to using recovery tools, you’ll find easy steps to help you get
those deleted Instagram videos and photos back.
Let’s walk through the process and get your content restored!
Way 1: Recover Deleted Videos from Instagram’s “Recently Deleted”
Folder
When you accidentally delete a video, Instagram has your back with the Recently Deleted folder.
It holds onto any photos, videos, reels, or stories you delete for 30 days before permanently wiping them
out. This gives you enough time to bring back anything you didn’t mean to delete.
Why It Works: Instagram created the Recently Deleted feature to help users recover content that was
deleted by mistake. Whether it’s deleted photos, deleted Instagram videos, or other content, you can
restore these items if you act quickly within that 30-day window.
Preparing to Restore a Deleted Video:
To show you how recovery works, I’ll start by deleting a video from my Instagram.

After deleting, Instagram shows a quick prompt letting me know that my video is safely put in storage in
the Recently Deleted folder for 30 days before it’s permanently removed.

Now, let’s move on to the recovery steps.
Steps to Recover a Deleted Video:
 Open the Instagram App: Start by opening your Instagram app on your Android device.
 Go to Your Profile: Tap on your profile icon located at the bottom-right of the screen. This will
take you to your profile page, where you can access additional options.
 Open the Menu: On your profile page, tap the three horizontal lines in the top-right corner. This
will open the menu with various options for managing your account.

 Select "Your Activity": From the menu options, tap on Your Activity. This section provides tools
to review and manage your Instagram activity, including access to recently deleted items.

 Open the "Recently Deleted" Folder: Inside Your Activity, scroll down to find and select
Recently Deleted. This opens a list of all content you’ve recently deleted from your profile,
including photos, videos, reels, and stories from the past 30 days.
 Select the Video: This will open the video in full view, giving you access to additional options.
 Restore the Video: Tap on the three dots in the bottom-right corner and select Restore. This
will initiate the process of recovering the video to your profile or gallery.

 Confirm Your Identity: For security, Instagram may ask you to verify your identity before
restoring the video. You’ll be prompted to choose a verification method, like receiving a code
via email or SMS. Select your preferred method and tap Next.

 Enter the Verification Code: Check your email or SMS for the six-digit code from Instagram.
Enter this code on the Instagram app and tap Confirm to complete the restoration.

 Video Restored: After successful verification, Instagram will restore the video to your profile or
gallery (depending on its original location). You’ll see a confirmation message, and your video
will be available for viewing or sharing once again.
Limitations: Once the 30-day period is up, Instagram will permanently delete the video, and you won’t
be able to recover it. So, act quickly before your content is gone for good!
Way 2: Recover Deleted Instagram Videos Using Your Phone’s Gallery or
File Manager
When you delete a video from Instagram, there’s still a chance that your phone saved a copy in its
gallery or file manager.
Many devices automatically save photos and videos, so it's worth checking these places to see if your
video is still there.
Why It Works: Some phones are set up to save every video and photo to the device’s internal storage. So,
even if you deleted it from Instagram, you might find the video stored in your phone’s gallery or file
manager.
For Android Users:
 Open the File Manager: Start by locating and opening the File Manager app on the Android
device. You can usually find it by searching for "File Manager" or "My Files" in your app
drawer.

 Access All Files: In the File Manager, go to All Files or Internal Storage to view your phone’s
internal storage folders.

 Navigate to the Pictures Folder: Once inside Internal storage, look for the Pictures folder.
Inside Pictures, locate the Instagram folder, where Instagram may have saved copies of videos
and images.

 Find the Deleted Video: Open the Instagram folder and browse to see if your deleted video is
still there. If it’s available, you can move or copy it back to your main gallery for easy access.

It’s pretty much the same process for iPhone users, though the steps are slightly different.
For iPhone Users:
 Open the Photos App: Launch the Photos app on the iPhone.
 Go to Recently Deleted: Tap Albums, then go to Recently Deleted. iPhone stores deleted photos
and videos here for 30 days.
 Recover the Video: Find the video you want, tap on it, and choose Recover to move it back to
your gallery.
Limitations: This method only works if the video was saved to your phone before it was deleted from
Instagram. If it wasn’t, you’ll need to try other methods to recover your lost photos or videos.
Way 3: Recover Deleted Instagram Videos Using the Archive Feature
If you’ve turned on Instagram’s Archive feature, there’s a good chance your deleted videos are still safe
in either the Posts Archive or Stories Archive.
This is a feature that automatically saves your posts and stories, so even if you delete something from
your Instagram account, it might still be waiting for you in the archive.
Why It Works: The Archive feature stores deleted content, but only if it was enabled before the deletion.
This means you can recover your deleted Instagram videos or deleted Instagram photos with ease. It’s a
built-in backup system that can help you recover deleted photos or videos when you think they’re gone.
Here’s how to recover deleted Instagram videos using the Archive feature:
 Open the Instagram App: Log in to your Instagram account and open the app.
 Go to Your Profile: Tap on your profile icon, sited at the bottom right of your screen, to access
your profile.

 Access the Archive: In the profile view, tap on the three lines in the top-right corner to open the
menu, then select Archive from the dropdown list.

 Browse for Archived Content: In the Archive section, you can switch between posts and stories
by selecting the dropdown at the top. Look through these to locate the deleted video.

 Restore the Video: Once you find the video you’re looking for, tap on it to view it. Then, choose
the option to either restore or repost it, which will bring the video back to your profile or story
feed.


Limitations: This method only works if the Archive feature was enabled before the video was deleted. If
the feature wasn’t turned on, the video will not be stored in the archive.
Way 4: Recover Deleted Videos Using Cloud Backups (Google Photos or
iCloud)
If your phone backs up photos and videos to a cloud service like Google Photos for Android or iCloud for
iPhone, your deleted Instagram video might still be available. This is because these backups often store
your media even after you’ve deleted it from the app.
Why It Works: Automatic cloud backups save your media files regularly. Even if you’ve deleted the video
from Instagram or you have deleted Instagram pictures, it might still be backed up in your cloud storage
so that you can restore it.
For Android (Google Photos):
 Open Google Photos: Launch the Google Photos app on your Android device by searching for
"Google Photos" in your app drawer.

 Search by Date: Look for the video by the date it was uploaded to Instagram. If Google Photos
automatically backs up your videos, it should appear in the list of photos and videos organized
by date.

 Recover the Video: Select the video, and you’ll have the option to share it directly to your
Instagram story or reel.

For iPhone users, the recovery process through iCloud is similar.
For iPhone (iCloud):
 Open iCloud: Go to the iCloud app or website.
 Check the Backup: Browse through recent backups or go directly to the Photos section to find
your video.
 Recover the Video: Once located, download or restore the video to your device.
Limitations: This method only works if automatic backups were enabled before the video was deleted. If
backups weren’t set up, there won’t be any deleted files or lost photos to recover.
Setting up automatic backups on cloud services is an easy way to ensure you don’t lose important media
like deleted Instagram videos. Always make sure you have backups enabled to protect your content.
Way 5: Recover Deleted Videos Using Third-Party Recovery Software
If your Instagram video was permanently deleted and you couldn’t find it in Instagram’s Recently Deleted
folder or cloud backups, third-party recovery software like EaseUS or Stellar Recovery might be your next
best option.
Software like Stellar Photo Recovery is designed to restore videos, deleted Instagram posts, and even
restore Instagram photos from internal storage.
These tools scan your device’s internal storage to help restore deleted Instagram videos, deleted images,
and other files that might not be easily accessible.
Why It Works: When a video is deleted, the data doesn’t vanish immediately from your device. Recovery
software can scan your phone’s storage to locate these files and bring them back.
The third-party recovery software I’m using is Stellar Data Recovery for Android. Here’s a simple step-by-
step guide on how I went about it:
Step 1: Install Stellar Data Recovery Software
a). Download and Install the Software: First, I downloaded Stellar Data Recovery for Android onto my
computer. During installation, I simply followed the setup wizard prompts.

Here’s the setup screen where I clicked "Next" to continue.

Once the installation was done, I clicked "Finish" to launch the software.

Step 2: Set Up Stellar Recovery for Video Retrieval
b). Open the Software and Choose What to Recover: After launching the Stellar Data Recovery software,
the first screen allows you to specify what type of data you want to recover.
Since I’m focused on retrieving a deleted video, I selected the "Videos" option.

Once I selected the video recovery option, I hit "Next" to proceed to the phone preparation and
connection steps.
Step 3: Prepare Your Phone
c). Enable USB Debugging: To let the software access my phone’s internal files, I had to turn on USB
Debugging. Here’s how:
 I went to Settings > About Phone > tapped Build Number seven times (this unlocks Developer
Options).
 Then, I opened Developer Options in Settings and switched on USB Debugging.


 Plug Your Android Phone into Your Computer: After enabling USB debugging, I connected my
phone to the computer using a USB cable. The software instantly recognized my device.
Step 4: Scan for Deleted Videos
d). Device Connection Confirmation: Once connected, Stellar will detect your device and show a
confirmation screen.


e). Start Scanning: Click "Scan" to start searching for deleted video files.

The software begins to scan your device. This may take a few minutes or hours, depending on the
storage size.

Step 5: Preview and Select the Video Files to Recover
f). Scan Complete Notification: Once the scan finishes, you’ll see a confirmation pop-up indicating that
the scan is complete.

g). View Scan Results: Once the scan is completed, you’ll get a list of recoverable files categorized by file
type. Scroll to the "Videos" section.



h). Select Your Video: Find and select the video you want to recover by checking the box next to it.
i). Choose Recovery Location: When you’re ready, choose where to save the recovered video on your
computer.


Step 7: Recover and Save
j). Begin Recovery: After selecting the file and the save location, click “Save” to start the recovery
process.
k). Recovery Progress: A progress bar will indicate the recovery process as the software saves the video
to your chosen location.

l). Access the Recovered File: Once the recovery is complete, go to the folder where you saved the video
to access your recovered file.
And that’s it! Stellar Data Recovery for Android helps you retrieve deleted videos that might not be
recoverable through standard options.
Limitations: Some recovery tools may require your phone to be rooted (Android) or jailbroken (iPhone)
to access deeper system files. This can be a little technical, so it’s worth checking the requirements
before starting.
Way 6: Use a Video Downloader to Recover Deleted Videos (If Still
Available Online)
If your deleted Instagram video is still viewable online—whether in a public post or an Instagram story—
you can use a third-party video downloader to save it back to your device. This method is useful when
the video is still accessible but not available on your profile.
Why It Works: As long as the video hasn’t been removed from Instagram’s servers and is still available to
view (e.g., shared as a post or story), you can use a video downloader to grab the file and save it to your
device. It's a quick and easy way to recover deleted Instagram posts or stories if they’re still visible.
Here’s how to recover deleted videos using a downloader:
a). Find a Downloader: Choose a third-party tool like DownloadGram or InstaSave. These tools let you
download Instagram videos to your device.


b). Copy the Video URL:
 Open the Instagram app and go to the post or story where the video was originally shared.
 Click on the three dots in the top-right corner to open the menu.
 Select the copied Instagram link to get the video URL.

c). Paste the URL:
 Go to the downloader website (such as DownloadGram or InstaSave).
 Paste the copied Instagram URL into the input box provided on the website.

d). Download the Video:
 After pasting the URL, click on the Download button to start processing the video.
 Once the download button appears, click Download again to save the video to your device.


e). Access the Video:
 Once downloaded, the video will be available in your phone’s gallery or Downloads folder for
easy access.


Limitations: This only works if the video is still available on Instagram. If it’s been removed from the
platform or taken down, this method won’t work.
Way 7: Contact Instagram Support (Last Resort)
If none of the earlier methods worked, reaching out to Instagram Support might be your last hope.
This option is most useful when your videos were deleted because of account issues like hacking or app
bugs. While it’s not guaranteed, it’s worth a try, especially if the video holds important memories or
valuable content.
Why It Works: If the video was deleted due to a technical glitch or a problem with your Instagram
account, the support team might be able to access data that users normally can’t recover themselves.
It’s also a good option if your account was compromised and someone else deleted the content.
Steps to Contact Instagram Support:
 Submit a Support Request: Open the Instagram Help Center in the app or on the website. Look
for the option to report a problem or get support.
 Explain the Issue: Be as clear and detailed as possible when describing your problem. Include
information like when the video was deleted, your username, and any other details that could
help the support team understand the situation.
 Wait for a Response: Once your request is submitted, wait for Instagram to review it. They will
get back to you with instructions or let you know if the video can be recovered.

Limitations: Instagram rarely recovers content that has been deleted beyond the Recently Deleted
period, but this is your final option for recovering important videos.
If you’re trying to figure out how To recover deleted videos from Instagram video downloader, contacting
support is a last resort when all other methods have failed.
Did You Get Your Videos Back?
I hope you’ve managed to recover your deleted Instagram videos by now!
Whether you used the Recently Deleted folder, a recovery app, or even reached out to Instagram
support, these methods can really save the day when videos vanish.
The key takeaway here is to act fast—don’t wait too long, or the chances of recovery might slip away.
To avoid going through this again, remember to back up your videos regularly and enable the Archive
feature on Instagram. It’s always better to have a backup than to stress over lost content.
Now, you’re all set to keep your Instagram content safe!

title: How To Add Pinterest HTML Tag To WordPress
content:
How To Add Pinterest HTML Tag To WordPress (Step By
Step)
"Find out how to add Pinterest HTML tag to WordPress with these easy steps. Get your site Pinterest-
ready in no time!"

You know, Pinterest is no longer just a place to save cute DIYs and recipe ideas.
According to Statista, Pinterest is now the fifteenth biggest search engine, with over 498 million active
users. Pretty impressive, right?


While Pinterest might not be as big as some social media giants, it’s still a powerful tool.
If you’ve added your website to Pinterest, that’s great news! It means you can drive more traffic from
Pinterest to your site.
But here’s the catch: if you don’t claim your WordPress website on Pinterest, your content can be shared
widely without giving you any credit whatsoever.
Claiming your website on Pinterest is a very simple way to verify that you are, in fact, the owner of that
website, and doing this can make you get access to several other tools like Pinterest analytics, ads
programs, stats for your photos, and many more.
This is what you stand to gain when someone saves an image from your claimed website:
 Your profile picture will show up next to the Pin.
 The Pin will link directly to your Pinterest profile.

 People will have the option to follow you on Pinterest.
So you can see that there are so many benefits that come with claiming your website on Pinterest, and
today, I am going to help you with this by showing you a step-by-step guide on how to add Pinterest
HTML tag to WordPress.
Whether you're a blogger, a small business owner, or just love sharing ideas on Pinterest, this guide will
help you link your Pinterest account to your site.
So, let's get started!
Is it Necessary That You Verify Your WordPress Site on Pinterest?
Pinterest is where people look for new ideas and inspiration or learn something through visuals.
With around so many active users, it’s a popular place for sharing and discovering images, GIFs, and
videos.
If your website features visual content—like photography or an online store—Pinterest can help increase
your web traffic and make your brand more visible.
By verifying your website on Pinterest, you’ll get insights into who’s visiting your site through Pinterest
Analytics.
Plus, you’ll be able to join their ad program and create a plan to grow your Pinterest traffic.
What is a Pinterest HTML Tag?

The Pinterest meta tag is a small piece of code you put on your website. It helps Pinterest see what
people do on your site after they click on your ads.

Here’s how it works: When you use this tag, Pinterest can track what visitors do on your site after seeing
your Pinterest ads. This means you get to see exactly how well your ads are performing and what actions
people take.
With the Pinterest tag, you can:
 Track and improve conversions: Find out how well your ads lead to actions on your site.
 Measure how your ads perform: See how effective your ads are.
 Create specific audiences: Target the right people with your ads.
 Become a verified merchant: Show that your site is trustworthy.
 Get insights into conversions: Get to know what happens after people interact with your ads.
For even better tracking, you can also use the Pinterest Conversions API along with the tag. It gives you
extra details about how your ads are working.
That being said, let’s see how you can easily verify your WordPress blog on Pinterest.
How to Add Pinterest HTML Tag to Your WordPress Site
There are several ways to connect your website to Pinterest, but this method is one of the fastest and
easiest ways.
Let’s take a look at what you need to do
Step 1. Upgrade Your Pinterest Account to Business
First, you need to upgrade your personal account to a business Pinterest account.
The Pinterest business account will give you access to many benefits, like increasing your brand’s
authority, driving traffic, creating and displaying ads, and getting Pinterest insights.
The good news is that setting up a Pinterest Business account is free and easy.
Since all Pinterest accounts start as personal, you’ll need to switch to a business account to claim your
website on Pinterest.
This is what you need to do.
Go to your Pinterest tab, sign in to your account, and click the arrow at the top right corner. Then, select
“Convert to business.”


On the next screen, you'll see a list of features that come with the business account.
To upgrade and start using these features, click the ‘Upgrade’ button.


After clicking on the upgrade button, Pinterest will now ask you to describe what kind of business your
account is for.

After that, fill in your business account details, such as your profile name, website URL, country, and
language.
Once you've done this, you can click on the button that says “Next.”


On the next screen, Pinterest will ask you to select an option for customized recommendations.
Once you have done this, make sure you click the ‘Done’ button.

Next, Pinterest will show you different options for getting started with your business account.
Here, we can see three options, including sharing ideas, growing your audience, and showcasing your
brand.


Now, let’s move to the next step and see how you can quickly and easily claim your WordPress website
on Pinterest.
Step 2: Claim Your Website on Pinterest
To claim your website, go to the "Settings" option. Then, head over to the "Claimed account" section and
click on it.
Here, you will see options to claim websites, such as Instagram and Shopify, but you would have to install
the Shopify app to claim on Pinterest.

When you click the claim button, a popup window will open with three ways to claim your WordPress
website.

Another option is to add a verification TXT record to your domain settings through your domain registrar.
(I will still cover these other options much later in this blog post).
Then, pick the “Add HTML tag” option.

If you prefer, you can choose to download the HTML file and upload it to your WordPress website’s root
directory using an FTP client, or you can use your WordPress hosting file manager.
Step 3: Add the HTML Tag to Your WordPress Website
There are various ways to add an HTML tag to your website’s header, but I will only cover the two easiest
methods.
a). Add the Pinterest Tag with an SEO plugin
You can make use of any SEO plugin for this, but here, I used the All in One SEO (AIOSEO) plugin, and all
you have to do is install this plugin on your WordPress Website.
Once you are done with the plugin installation, you can now verify your site with Pinterest using the
WebMaster Tools feature.
To do so, just go to the WordPress Dashboard>>General Setting>>WebMaster Tools and then click on the
Pinterest Site Verification.


Once you have selected this, the verification tab will appear on the same screen.
Here, you would need to copy the code you saw on Pinterest when you clicked on the “Add HTML tag”
and paste it into the Pinterest verification code.

All you have to do now is click the “Save Changes” button.
b). Add the Pinterest HTML Tag With a Code Snippets Plugin
Apart from using the AIOSEO plugin, you can add the HTML tag by installing and activating another
plugin called the WPCode plugin.
When you want to activate this plugin, all you have to do is go to the Code Snippets >> Header & Footer
section in your WordPress dashboard.
In the “Header section,” you have to paste the HTML tag you got from Pinterest and then click the “Save
Changes” button.


The moment the HTML code is added to your website’s Header section, you have to go back to where
you left off on Pinterest and click the “Continue” button.


The next stage is the verification process. Pinterest will require that you enter the URL of your website
and then click on the “Verify “ button.
This is to verify your WordPress website.


After that, you’ll see a message saying, “Verification in progress.”
It will take a few seconds to complete. Once it’s done, you’ll see a message confirming that you’re
verified.

If everything goes well, you’ll see a "Connected" message with a green checkmark.
That’s it! Just click the Done button.


Finally! Your website has been claimed successfully.
Note: If Pinterest fails to verify your account after you have added the verification code, then you have to
clear your WordPress cache
Other Ways to Verify Your WordPress Website on Pinterest
If you don’t feel comfortable adding the HTML tag to your website's header, as provided by Pinterest,
there are two other ways you can verify your WordPress website
Let's take a look at them!
a). Upload the Custom HTML File to Your WordPress root Folder
Pinterest also enables you to verify your website by uploading an HTML file (provided by them) to your
website’s root folder on your server.
The difference between the first method we discussed, which is using an HTML tag, is that you will
upload the entire file to your website directory instead of just updating the current file with a piece of
code.
As a WordPress user, I am sure you have probably already found your way to your WordPress root folder
to make changes more than once, so this process should be easy.

Step 1: Go to the Claimed Section on Your Pinterest Account
To get started, return to your Pinterest settings screen and go once again to the Claim section. Add your
website’s URL, and you choose which claim option you want to use.
This time, we’re going to choose the Upload HTML file option and then click the download button. This
downloads the HTML file wherever you want to save it on your computer.
The name of the file starts with “Pinterest,” but you can change the name to whatever you like.

Step 2: Upload the HTML File to Your Site’s Server Using an FTP Client
After downloading the file, open your FTP client (I’m using FileZilla), find the Pinterest HTML file on your
computer, and drag it into the root folder of your WordPress site.
The “root” folder can be different depending on the kind of platform you are using, but for WordPress,
it’s usually the /public folder.
Once you find the root folder, you should see a list of files and directories like this:

This will start the upload process, which should only take a few seconds since the file is small.
Once it’s done, you can close FileZilla. The next step is to verify your account. It is the same verification
method that was used when we were “Adding HTML meta tag” on Pinterest.
Note: If you are having trouble connecting with your account via this method, it’s most likely because you
are not using the root folder. As I mentioned before, you can typically expect most WordPress sites to use
/public as the root folder, but that is not always the case, so make sure to search for your root folder.
b). Add the TXT Record to Your Domain Host
This method is different because it involves your DNS (Domain Name Service) registrar instead of using
WordPress files.
So, instead of adding the HTML tags or files, you’ll add a TXT record.
To do this, you need to log in to your domain provider account (which is often your hosting provider,
though not always).
For this example, I’m using Kinsta and have already added a third-party domain to my account for this
process.
Here is how to go about it
Step 1: Go to the Your Claimed Account Section on Pinterest
Select the option to “Add TXT Record,” copy the TXT record to your clipboard, and then click the
Continue button.

Step 2: Log into Your DNS Provider Account
Access your domain name provider’s dashboard and log in. Add the new DNS TXT record and save it to
your account.
In MyKinsta, go to the Kinsta DNS section and select the domain you want to use.


Step 3: Add a New DNS TXT Record
Scroll down to find the DNS Records section. Then, click the button to Add a DNS Record.

Select the TXT tab. Keep the Hostname and TTL fields as they are. Paste the Pinterest TXT record you
copied earlier into the Content field. Then, click the Add DNS button.


You should now see the TXT record saved successfully in your list of DNS records.

Next, go back to your Pinterest dashboard and paste your site URL into the Verify field. Click the Verify
button to proceed.
If it works, you’ll see a “Connected” message with a green checkmark. Click Done and move on to check
all your new features as a verified Pinterest business!


Tips for Troubleshooting Common Issues

Even with these instructions, you might run into some hiccups when adding the Pinterest HTML tag to
your WordPress site.
Don’t worry—these issues are usually easy to fix. Here are some common problems and how to solve
them:
1). Pinterest Verification Code Not Accepted
 Problem: Pinterest doesn’t accept the verification code you’ve added.
 Solution: Ensure you copied the exact code Pinterest provided. Sometimes, extra spaces or line
breaks can cause issues. Use a plain text editor to paste the code before adding it to your
WordPress site. Also, verify that you’re placing it in the section of your site’s HTML.
2). Tag Appears in Source Code but Not Verified
 Problem: The HTML tag appears in the source code, but Pinterest still doesn’t recognize it.
 Solution: Check if the tag is correctly placed in the section. If using a caching plugin (like
W3 Total Cache or WP Super Cache), clear the cache after adding the tag. Also, confirm you’re
looking at the correct site version if you have multiple domains or subdomains.
3). Tag Added, but Verification Still Fails
 Problem: After adding the tag, Pinterest fails verification repeatedly.
 Solution: Make sure there are no syntax errors or typos in the tag. Sometimes, security plugins
or server settings may block Pinterest from reading the tag. Temporarily disable such plugins or
adjust settings to allow Pinterest access, then try verifying again.
4). Using a Child Theme and Tag Missing
 Problem: The tag isn’t showing up when using a child theme.

 Solution: Ensure you’ve added the tag to the header.php file of the child theme, not the parent
theme. WordPress can sometimes prioritize the files of the parent theme over the child theme.
Double-check the correct file path and placement.
5). HTML Tag Appearing in Footer
 Problem: The Pinterest HTML tag appears in the footer instead of the header.
 Solution: If you’re using a plugin or custom code to add the tag, ensure it’s set to insert in the
header. Some plugins have settings that let you choose the location for code snippets. Adjust
these settings to ensure the tag is placed in the correct section.
6). Problems with Plugin-Based Methods
 Problem: The plugin you used to insert the Pinterest tag isn’t working.
 Solution: Check for plugin conflicts by deactivating other plugins and seeing if the issue resolves.
Make sure the plugin you are using is updated to the latest version. If problems persist, consider
switching to another plugin or method to insert the tag.
7). Verification Code Not Showing on HTTPS Sites
 Problem: Pinterest can’t verify the tag on a site with HTTPS.
 Solution: Ensure the HTML tag is being added to the secure version of your site. Check if your
site has a mixed content issue where HTTP and HTTPS elements are mixed. Use browser
developer tools to inspect if the tag appears correctly on the secure version.
8). Issues with DNS TXT Record for Domain Verification
 Problem: The TXT record for domain verification isn’t working.
 Solution: Make sure the TXT record is added correctly in your domain’s DNS settings.
Sometimes, DNS changes take up to 48 hours to propagate. Check the DNS settings with your
domain registrar and ensure there are no typos or errors in the TXT record.
9). Browser Cache Preventing Updates
 Problem: Your browser cache might be showing outdated information.
 Solution: Clear your browser’s cache and cookies. Try opening your website with a different
browser or incognito mode to see if the tag appears. Sometimes, cached versions of your site
might not reflect recent changes.
10). Theme Conflicts
 Problem: The tag is not appearing due to theme conflicts.
 Solution: Temporarily change your theme to a default WordPress one, like Twenty Twenty-One,
to see if the issue is resolved. If it does, the problem may be with your theme. Contact the
theme developer for assistance or check the theme’s settings for options related to header
content.
11). Tag Verification Issues with Multi-Site Networks
 Problem: Verification fails on a WordPress multi-site network.

 Solution: Ensure the tag is added to the correct site within the network. In multi-site setups,
each site may need its own verification tag. Add the tag to each individual site’s header or
configure network-wide settings if supported.
12). Issues with Custom Code Implementations
 Problem: Custom code implementations cause problems with the Pinterest tag.
 Solution: Review the custom code for errors or conflicts. Test the tag with minimal code to
ensure it’s working, then gradually reintroduce other code elements. This helps isolate any
conflicts or issues.
By following these tips, you should be able to resolve common issues and ensure that your Pinterest
HTML tag is properly set up.
If you continue to face problems, don’t hesitate to reach out to Pinterest support or your WordPress
hosting provider for further assistance.
What To Do After Claiming Your Website On Pinterest
Once you see the “Connected” message, it usually means your website is claimed on Pinterest.
However, there are a few extra steps to make sure everything is set up correctly. Sometimes, you might
also need to wait for a verification email from Pinterest.
Here are five steps to take next:
1). Check to Make Sure Your Website is Verified
Confirm that your website is indeed claimed on Pinterest. Go to Settings > Claimed Accounts, and look
under the Websites section. If you see your domain listed there, it means your website is successfully
claimed.
2). Look for a Verification Email
Sometimes, you might need to wait for a verification email from Pinterest.
If you see a “Verification in progress” message, it means Pinterest is still processing your claim. This
might take a few hours or even days. Keep an eye on your email for updates from Pinterest.
3). Review Your Pinterest Profile
Ensure your Pinterest profile is updated with your website link and looks professional.
4). Make use of Pinterest Analytics
Check Pinterest Analytics to see how your content is performing and gather insights about your
audience.
5). Set Up Pinterest Ads
Consider setting up Pinterest Ads to drive more traffic and promote your content.

6). Monitor Your Website’s Performance
Watch how your website is performing with Pinterest traffic and adjust your strategy as needed.
Final Thoughts

You’ve made it to the end!
Can you see that adding the Pinterest HTML tag to your WordPress site is a simple yet powerful step to
increase your online presence?
By claiming your website on Pinterest, you ensure that your content is linked directly to you, which
means more control and better insights into your audience. Plus, it’s a great way to increase your site’s
visibility and drive more traffic your way.
Here’s a quick recap:
 Upgrade to a Pinterest Business Account – It’s free and opens up lots of helpful tools.
 Claim Your Website – Choose the easiest method for you, whether it’s adding an HTML tag,
uploading a file, or adding a TXT record.
 Verify Your Website – Make sure everything is set up correctly and check for a confirmation
message.
I hope your website has now been verified on Pinterest, and you can now use all those amazing features
that come with a Pinterest Business account.
With these steps, you’re all set to make the most out of Pinterest’s features and drive more engagement
to your site.

Her Purpose, His Plan: A
Woman’s Journey with God
Chapter 1: Purpose in Childhood and Adolescence
"Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you, before you
were born, I set you apart." – Jeremiah 1:5
Have you ever read that verse and just felt like it was speaking
directly to you? I know I have.
Every time I read it, it hits me all over again: God had a plan for
me before I even existed.
Before I could walk, talk, or even think, He had already mapped
out my purpose.
Let that sink in for a moment—before anyone else knew you,
God already did, and He had something special in mind for you.
And guess what? Being born a girl wasn’t an accident. God
didn’t flip a coin or leave it up to chance.
He created you with intention. There were times growing up
when I wondered if maybe He got it wrong.
Maybe I wasn’t enough or didn’t fit into the "big plan" as
much as someone else. But trust me, He knew exactly what He
was doing when He made you the way you are.

Who Am I Supposed to Be?
I remember being around 14—right in the middle of that phase
where you’re not a kid anymore, but you’re definitely not an
adult.
You’re somewhere in between, trying to figure out where you
fit.
I had friends who seemed like they had it all together: the
super popular girl, the one who was always top of the class.
And then there was me, feeling like I was floating somewhere
in the middle.
I didn’t really know who I was supposed to be, and it felt like
everyone else already had it figured out.
One night, I was lying in bed, staring at the ceiling, and it hit
me—I had no clue who I was. It was kind of overwhelming.
My mind started racing with all these thoughts:
"Am I doing this right?
Am I enough?
What does God even want from me?"
I talked to my mom about it the next day. She’s always been my
go-to when I’m feeling lost.

She said something that really stuck with me: “God made you
exactly the way He wanted to. You don’t need to be like
anyone else. You’re supposed to be you.”
At first, I didn’t get it. I mean, how many times have we heard
people say, “Be yourself”? But as I thought about it more, I
realized she was right.
I wasn’t created to blend in with everyone else. Neither were
you.
God already knows who you are, and He doesn’t want you to
copy anyone else’s life. He has a unique purpose just for you.
The Messy Middle
Let’s be real— being a teenager is chaotic. It’s confusing. There
are days when you feel like you’re on top of the world, and
then there are days when nothing seems to make sense.
It’s like you’re stuck between childhood and adulthood, and
you’re not really sure where you fit. I’ve been there. I think
we’ve all been there.
It’s easy to feel like you’re not enough or like you don’t
measure up to what the world expects.
But here’s something I’ve learned: God doesn’t
need you to have everything figured out. He’s

God reveals His plan for us one step at a time, and sometimes,
all we can do is take a small step of faith and trust Him with the
rest.

biggest responsibility ever. She didn’t have all the answers, but

she said yes. She trusted God, even though she couldn’t see
the whole picture.

know the end of the story yet.

something amazing in store for you.

out yet. God is still working on you, and that’s a good thing.

discovering who you are in His eyes.

important: God’s timing is perfect, even when it doesn’t match
ours.
We want answers now, but He’s always working behind the
scenes, shaping us for something greater.
The key is to stay close to Him, trust the process, and know
that even when things seem uncertain, He’s got a plan.
I didn’t understand it at the time, but those awkward years of
feeling lost, confused, and unsure of who I was meant to be
were actually part of God’s plan to help me grow.

Every experience, every moment of doubt, was leading me
closer to understanding my true purpose. It wasn’t always easy,
but looking back, I can see how He was preparing me for the
next chapter of my life.

have everything figured out right now. It’s okay to feel
uncertain—it’s part of the journey.
Trust that God is with you in every step, even when the path
ahead seems unclear. He’s writing your story, and trust me, it’s

feeling lost, just like I was when I was her age.

answers.

now. Take it one day at a time, pray, and trust that God will
show you the way.”

that you are seen, known, and loved by the One who created
you. He’s got you, and He’s not in a hurry.
Let Him take you on this journey, step by step. You don’t have
to rush into the next stage of life—just lean into the moment,

grow where you are, and trust that in His perfect timing,

trusted God with their purpose, even when they didn’t
have all the answers.

plan will unfold in His timing.

things one step at a time. Each step you take is part of

Chapter 3: Purpose in Career, Relationships, and Ministry
I remember reading a book by Joyce Meyer called Living
Beyond Your Feelings.

everyday life—whether it’s in our work, relationships, or acts of
service.

lives with God’s will, we find true fulfillment.”

relationships, and ministries aren’t just random parts of our
lives. They’re pieces of a bigger plan that God has for each of
us.
But finding that purpose doesn’t always feel easy. It can feel
like we’re walking through life, but we're not sure of the full
picture.
However, by taking small, thoughtful steps and leaning on
prayer and reflection, we start to see how the different pieces
fit into God’s bigger plan for our lives.
"Is This the Right Path for My Career?"

struggle with.
We often ask ourselves, “Am I doing what I’m supposed to be
doing?” or

“Is this job part of God’s plan for me, or should I be doing
something else?”
Before we answer those questions, let’s remember that God
works through us in all kinds of ways.
The job you have right now, even if it feels ordinary or
unexciting, may still serve a bigger purpose.
But how do you know if it’s time to make a change or if you’re
already where God wants you to be?
It’s important to pause and think about what parts of your
work give you joy.
Are there moments in your job that make you feel happy or
fulfilled?
Can you do more of those things in your current role?
Or maybe God is gently guiding you toward something new
that aligns better with your gifts.
A few months ago, I had a long conversation with my friend
Solene.
We’d been close for years, but life had been busy, and we
hadn’t caught up properly in a while.
One day, we met up for brunch, and right away, I could tell
something was weighing on her.

Solene: I’ve been feeling really stuck lately. Like, I don’t know
why I’m doing what I’m doing anymore.

deeper—this feeling of dissatisfaction with her career that had
been building for months.

Solene: Yeah. It’s not that I hate it. It’s just... I don’t know if I’m

teaching, but now I feel like I’m just going through the motions.

everything she did, so hearing her question her path was a bit

Me: You’ve been teaching for years, and you’ve always loved it.

Solene: Maybe both? I don’t know. I just don’t feel like I’m

place.


Me: Do you remember why you got into teaching in the first

Solene: Yeah... I always loved helping people learn. Watching a
student finally "get it" after struggling with something—that
used to light me up. But now, it feels like I’m just ticking boxes
and dealing with admin stuff all day.
Me: So, what if the problem isn’t teaching itself, but how you’re
teaching right now?
She looked at me, eyebrows raised, as if I’d just said something
revolutionary.
Solene: What do you mean?
Me: Maybe it’s not that you’re in the wrong career, but that
you need to find a way to bring your passion back into it. What
part of your job do you still enjoy?
She thought for a moment before responding.
Solene: I love the one-on-one time with students, helping them
figure out how to approach something they’re stuck on. But I
hardly get to do that anymore.

day? Maybe there’s a way to shift things around. Or perhaps
you could even start something new—like tutoring or leading
smaller workshops that focus on that one-on-one interaction.


Solene: I’ve thought about it, but I don’t know if it’s realistic...

Solene: I guess I’m scared of change. What if it doesn’t work

sure.

His kingdom.

one flesh.”

front.

support and uplift each other.

communication and a willingness to adapt.

finances, family life, and personal growth.

planning and cooperation.

were on the same page about our budget and expenses.

communication and regularly checking in with each other, we

learned that compromise and flexibility were key to making it
work.
Building a Marriage That Reflects God’s Purpose
So, how do you build a marriage that’s grounded in God’s
purpose?
