Module 5: Living a Transformed Life
Welcome to Module 5!
We've been on quite a journey together, haven’t we? We've talked about pushing past our limits, finding
inner strength, trusting God’s timing, and building strength through action.
Now, it’s time to focus on what all of this work leads to—living a truly transformed life.
This is where all that hard work and faith come together, where you step into the woman God has been
shaping you to be.
So, let’s get started and see what it means to embrace this new you.

Embracing Your New Self
Let's start with the idea of change. Change can feel a little uncomfortable, right?
Think back to when you first started this course. Maybe you were unsure or even a little scared of what
might change.
But look at how far you’ve come! You’ve been growing, learning, and pushing through challenges. It’s so
important to recognize and accept the changes that have happened to you.
Sometimes, it’s tempting to hold on to the past versions of ourselves because they’re familiar. But God
calls us to embrace the new creation that we are becoming.
2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone,
the new is here!” You’re not the same person you were before. And that’s a good thing!
God is constantly at work, molding you into someone even more beautiful, more faithful, and more in
tune with His purpose.
I remember a time when I struggled with change. I was so set in my ways, thinking that if I just stayed the
same, I wouldn’t have to deal with the unknown. But God had other plans.
He gently nudged me, little by little, until I realized that staying the same wasn’t an option if I wanted to
grow closer to Him.
It was like peeling back layers of an onion—not always easy, sometimes it even stung—but necessary to
get to the heart of who He wanted me to be.
So, how are you feeling about the changes you’ve gone through? Maybe you’ve started praying more
regularly, or perhaps you’ve let go of some old habits that were holding you back.
Whatever it is, take a moment to acknowledge those changes. They are evidence of God’s hand at work
in your life.
Living with Purpose
Now that you’ve embraced the new you, it’s time to live with purpose.
Everything you’ve been through, every challenge you’ve faced, has been part of God’s plan to equip you
for the life you’re meant to live.
You’ve been learning not just for the sake of knowledge but to prepare you for the good works that God
has planned for you. This is your moment to step into that purpose with confidence.
Ephesians 2:10 tells us, “For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which
God prepared in advance for us to do.”
That means God has specific plans for you—yes, you!
He’s got work lined up that only you can do based on the unique gifts and experiences He’s given you.
Living with purpose doesn’t mean you have to have everything figured out. It simply means you’re
willing to walk in the direction God is leading you.

It’s about taking what you’ve learned and applying it to your daily life, making decisions that align with
the person you’re becoming.
It’s about letting your experiences shape your actions, your choices, and your impact on the world
around you.
There was a time when I felt so lost, unsure of what my purpose was. I kept asking God, “What do you
want me to do?” And the answer wasn’t immediate.
It took a lot of prayer, a lot of waiting, and a lot of small steps forward. But slowly, I began to see the
bigger picture.
God was preparing me through my everyday experiences—being a wife, a mother, and a friend. All those
moments I thought were ordinary were actually part of His extraordinary plan for me.
You see, living with purpose doesn’t always mean making grand gestures or taking giant leaps.
Sometimes, it’s in the little things—how you encourage a friend, how you raise your children, how you
serve in your community.
All of these are acts of purpose that God has set before you.
So, what are the things in your life that God might be using to prepare you for something bigger?
How can you start living out that purpose today?
Inspiring Others
Your journey doesn’t end with you. One of the most powerful ways to live out your transformation is by
sharing your story with others.
Revelation 12:11 says, “They triumphed over him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their
testimony.”
Your story has power, more than you might realize. Sharing what God has done in your life can
encourage someone else who’s struggling with the same things you’ve overcome.
I used to think my story wasn’t all that interesting.
I mean, who would want to hear about my ups and downs? But then I started sharing little bits and
pieces with friends, and I noticed something amazing—they were encouraged by my struggles and
victories.
It’s like when you’re climbing a mountain, and you see someone else who’s a few steps ahead. Their
journey gives you the strength to keep going, knowing that if they can make it, so can you.
So, who in your life could use a little encouragement right now?
Maybe it’s a friend going through a tough time or a family member who feels stuck.
Don’t be afraid to share your story with them. You never know how your experiences might be just what
they need to hear to keep moving forward.

Ongoing Growth
Even though you’ve made so much progress, the journey doesn’t stop here. Growth is a lifelong process.
Proverbs 1:5 tells us, “Let the wise listen and add to their learning, and let the discerning get
guidance.”
In other words, we never stop growing, learning, or seeking God’s wisdom.
Think of your spiritual growth as tending a garden. You don’t just plant seeds and walk away. You water
them, pull out the weeds, and make sure they get enough sunlight. The same goes for your spiritual life.
Keep feeding your spirit with God’s Word, stay connected to Him through prayer, and surround yourself
with people who encourage you to grow.
I’ve found that ongoing growth is key to staying grounded in my faith. Whether it’s through reading
scripture, seeking out new learning opportunities, or spending time in prayer, I’m always looking for
ways to grow closer to God.
One thing I love to do while I am growing is celebrate the little victories God gives me along the way. It
could be finishing a Bible study, seeing an answered prayer, or even just having a day where I felt God’s
peace more than usual.
These are the moments that remind me I’m on the right path, even when it doesn’t always feel like it.
So, take a moment to think about how far you’ve come. What milestones have you reached?
How has your relationship with God deepened over time?
And most importantly, how can you continue to grow and learn as you move forward?
Practical Actions
a). Celebrate Your Milestones
Take some time to acknowledge the progress you’ve made. It’s easy to get caught up in what’s next, but
celebrating your achievements, no matter how small, is important.
b). Continuous Learning
Keep investing in your personal and spiritual growth. Whether it’s through reading, prayer, or spending
time with others who uplift you, make sure you’re continually feeding your mind and spirit.
Questions to Reflect On
 How can you embrace and celebrate the growth and changes God has brought into your life?
 Who in your life could benefit from hearing your story, and how can you share it with them?
 What steps can you take to continue growing spiritually and personally?
Action Steps
 Reflect on your journey and write down the changes you’ve experienced. Consider journaling
about your transformation and thanking God for each step of the process.

 Share your story with someone who could benefit from it. It could be a friend, a family member,
or even someone in your church community.
 Celebrate your milestones. Whether it’s through prayer, a small gathering, or simply taking a
moment to thank God, make sure you acknowledge how far you’ve come.
Ladies, living a transformed life is an ongoing journey. Embrace the changes, live with purpose, and
never stop growing in your faith.
And remember, your story is powerful—don’t hesitate to share it with others. As you continue on this
path, may God bless you with strength, wisdom, and a heart full of love.
That’s all for Module 5!
Next, in Module 6, we’ll talk about how to find balance in your roles as a homemaker and a leader. We’ll
be looking at practical tips for managing your responsibilities, setting boundaries, and making sure you
have time for both your personal goals and your family.

Module 6: Balancing Your Roles as a Homemaker and Leader
Welcome to Module 6!
We are going to be talking about a topic that touches the heart of many Christian women: how to
balance being a homemaker while also taking on leadership roles.
It’s easy to feel overwhelmed with everything on our plates, but here’s the good news—with God’s help
and some tips I will be sharing that have worked well for me over the years, you can find a balance that
works for you.
Let’s get started!
Finding Balance
Balancing homemaking with leadership isn’t easy, but it’s possible.
As Christian women, we sometimes feel like we have to do everything perfectly—taking care of our
families, keeping our homes in order, and fulfilling our duties at church or work.
But God doesn’t ask for perfection; He asks for faithfulness in what He’s called us to do.
Think about the Proverbs 31 woman. She’s a wonderful example of someone who manages her home
with care while also engaging in business and helping others.
Proverbs 31:15-18 talks about how she gets up early to provide for her family and makes wise
investments.
She didn’t just wake up one day with everything figured out—she worked on it continuously.
Another woman we can learn one or two things from is Ruth, who worked diligently in the fields to
provide for her family while also showing love and loyalty to her mother-in-law, Naomi.
Ruth didn't let her responsibilities overwhelm her; instead, she approached each task with purpose and
dedication.
Just like these women, finding balance in your life takes effort.
It starts with recognizing that you don’t have to do everything. You need to prioritize what’s most
important and let go of the rest. It’s okay to ask for help or say no when you’re feeling stretched too thin.

I remember when my kids were younger, I tried to be the perfect mom, wife, and teacher at the
children’s church all at once.
I wanted to do it all, but eventually, I realized I was wearing myself out. It wasn’t until I started setting
boundaries and asking for help that I found a better balance. I had to learn that saying no to one thing
could mean saying yes to something more important.
Setting Boundaries
Next, let’s talk about boundaries. They’re so important in keeping you from getting overwhelmed and to
avoid burnout.
Have you ever felt like there just aren’t enough hours in the day? It can be tough to say no, especially
when we want to help everyone around us.
Philippians 4:13 reminds us that we can do all things through Christ, who strengthens us, but it doesn’t
mean we have to do everything.
Sometimes, it means recognizing your limits and setting boundaries to protect your well-being.
For example, maybe you need to set aside certain times in your day that are just for your family or just
for your personal time with God.
It’s okay to say no to extra commitments if they interfere with those priorities. Remember, even Jesus
took time away from the crowds to rest and pray (Mark 6:31).
In my own life, I’ve found that setting boundaries was key to finding balance. I used to feel guilty for
saying no, especially when it came to helping out at church.
But then I realized that if I were constantly worn out, I wouldn’t be any good to my family or to those I
was trying to help.
Setting boundaries isn’t about being selfish; it’s about being wise with the time and energy God has
given you.
Time Management
Another important thing that can help you find balance is time management. Here are a few simple
steps that have helped me:
a). Prioritize Your tasks
One of the most helpful things we can do is prioritize our tasks. Take a moment each day to list out what
you need to accomplish.
Focus on what’s truly important. It can be easy to get caught up in tasks that feel urgent but aren’t
necessarily important.
Try breaking your list into three categories:
 Must Do: These are the tasks that need your immediate attention.
 Should Do: These are important but can wait if necessary.

 Nice to Do: These are tasks you’d like to complete but aren’t essential right now.
2). Create a Flexible Schedule
It’s helpful to have a daily or weekly schedule, but it should be flexible. Leave room for unexpected
things that might come up, and don’t be too hard on yourself if everything doesn’t go as planned.
For this, you can use a planner or even a simple notebook. Set aside time for your homemaking tasks,
but also include time for your personal growth activities.
3). Include Self-Care
Make sure your schedule includes time for yourself. Whether it’s a quiet moment with God, a walk
outside, or a hobby you enjoy, self-care is important for keeping your mind and body healthy.
I used to think that self-care was a luxury I couldn’t afford, but I’ve since learned that it’s very necessary.
When I’m taking care of myself, I’m more patient, more joyful, and more effective in my roles as a
homemaker and leader.
Practical Tips
Here are some things to do that can help you balance your role:
a). Daily Planning
Spend a few minutes each evening planning for the next day. Review what you accomplished and set up
your to-do list for tomorrow.
Use a planner or an app to organize your daily tasks. Seeing everything laid out can help you stay focused
and reduce stress.
b). Self-Care
Don’t forget to make time for yourself.
Schedule a regular time for activities that refresh and energize you. It could be as simple as reading a
good book, taking a bath, or spending time in prayer.
c). Celebrate Small Wins
Don’t wait until everything is perfect to celebrate. Acknowledge your progress, no matter how small.
Each step forward is worth celebrating.
Questions to Think About
As you reflect on balancing your roles, here are some questions to ponder:
a). How do you balance your home duties with your personal and spiritual goals?
Reflect on your personal goals and think about how you can incorporate them into your daily routine. It’s
important to find a way to nurture both your responsibilities and your aspirations.
b). What boundaries can you set to avoid feeling overwhelmed?

Identify areas where you feel overextended and set clear boundaries. This might involve delegating tasks
or saying no to additional commitments.
Action Steps
To wrap up, here are some action steps to help you implement what we’ve discussed:
 Create a weekly schedule that includes both homemaking tasks and personal growth activities.
Make sure to include time for yourself and your family.
 Identify areas where you need to set boundaries and start making those changes. This might
involve reducing your commitments or finding additional support.
That’s all for module 6!
Remember, God has equipped you with everything you need to fulfill your roles. It’s not about doing it
all perfectly but about being faithful and trusting Him to guide you.
With prayer, planning, and a little bit of flexibility, you can find the balance that works for you. And when
you do, you’ll not only be a blessing to your family and community, but you’ll also find joy and fulfillment
in your everyday life.
In the next module, we’ll be talking about how to grow spiritually. We’ll cover how to include daily
devotions and prayer in your life, find opportunities for spiritual growth, and join faith groups.
I’m excited to share these insights with you and help you deepen your relationship with God. See you in

Module 7: Growing Spiritually
Hi there, welcome to Module 7
In this module, we're going to talk about growing spiritually and deepening your faith. It’s easy to get
caught up in the busyness of life, but making time for spiritual growth is so important.
We’ll look at some simple ways to include daily devotions, study the Bible, and find opportunities to
grow spiritually.
Let’s get started!
Deepening Your Faith
a). Daily Devotions
One of the best ways to grow spiritually is through daily devotions. This simply means setting aside time
each day to read a bit from the Bible and talk to God.
Even a few minutes each day can make a big difference. Psalm 119:105 says, “Your word is a lamp to my
feet and a light for my path.”
This verse reminds us that God’s word helps guide us through life, just like a flashlight helps us see in the
dark.
You don’t need to spend hours each day on this. Maybe start with 15-30 minutes in the morning or
before bed. Find a quiet spot where you can read a Bible verse or two, reflect on it, and say a prayer.
It could be as simple as asking for guidance for the day ahead or giving thanks for your blessings.
You might ask, “How do I fit this into my busy schedule?” Well, my advice for you is to start small.

Maybe you could begin with just 10 minutes a day. Read a verse, say a quick prayer, and gradually build
on it. It’s about consistency, not perfection.
As you get used to this routine, you’ll find it easier to make time for God, even on the busiest days.
b). Bible Study
Next up is Bible study.
Studying the Bible is a great way to grow in your faith. It’s not just about reading the words but really
understanding and applying them to your life.
One thing you can do to make this easier is to use a study guide or a devotional book that breaks down
passages and explains them in a way that makes sense to you.
One story that really touched me is the story of the woman at the well in John 4. Jesus meets a
Samaritan woman at a well and offers her “living water,” which represents eternal life.
Her encounter with Jesus transforms her life, and she goes on to share her story with others.
This story reminds us that spending time with Jesus and understanding His teachings can change our
lives and help us share His love with others.
Finding Spiritual Growth Opportunities
a). Joining a Group
Being part of a Bible study, faith group, or church can be incredibly helpful. It’s like having a group of
friends who are also on their spiritual journey, supporting and encouraging each other.
They can help you stay accountable and motivated in your walk with God. It’s also a great way to make
new connections with others who share your values.
I remember when I joined a women’s Bible study group at my church. At first, I was nervous, but it
quickly became a source of strength and inspiration.
We shared our struggles and victories, prayed for each other, and learned so much together. It was like
having a supportive family on my spiritual journey, and it has become a meaningful part of my week.
b). Serving Others
Serving others is another wonderful way to grow spiritually. When you volunteer or help out in your
community, you’re living out your faith in a tangible way.
Jesus taught us to love our neighbors and serve others, and doing so can strengthen your own faith.
Think about what you’re passionate about or where you see a need. Maybe you can help at a local food
bank, assist at a community event, or even just lend a hand to a neighbor in need. Every act of service,
big or small, reflects God's love and brings spiritual growth.



Practical Strategies
a). Prayer Journals
One simple tool that’s helped me is keeping a prayer journal. It’s just a notebook where I write down my
prayers and what I’m learning from the Bible. It’s a great way to keep track of my spiritual journey and
see how God is working in my life.
A simple notebook will help you get started. Write down your thoughts, prayers, and any insights you
gain. It’s a personal way to connect with God and track your spiritual growth.
b). Volunteer Work
Engaging in volunteer work is another great way to grow spiritually. Finding ways to help others in your
community can be both rewarding and enriching. It’s a way to use your talents and time for a good
cause, and it helps you grow in your faith.
Look for local charities or community events where you can lend a hand. Whether it’s organizing an
event, helping with a meal, or working on a project, your involvement will make a difference and help
you grow spiritually.
Questions to Think About
As you go through this module, here are a few questions to consider:
 How can you include daily devotions and prayer in your busy schedule? What time of day is best
for you to connect with God?
 What are some ways to serve others and grow spiritually? Think about where you can offer your
help and how serving others can bring you closer to God.
Action Steps
Here’s what you can do next:
 Set Aside Time: Choose a specific time each day for prayer and Bible study. Find a devotional or
study plan that you like and stick with it.
 Join a Group: Look for local or online faith groups to join. It’s a great way to find support and
community as you grow spiritually.
 Start a Prayer Journal: Begin keeping a journal where you write down your prayers and
reflections. It’s a wonderful way to track your spiritual journey.
 Engage in Volunteer Work: Find a volunteer opportunity that matches your interests and get
involved. Your time and efforts will not only help others but also enrich your own faith.
That’s all for module 7.
Growing spiritually is a journey, not a destination. It’s about making small, consistent changes that help
you deepen your relationship with God.

As we wrap up Module 7, I encourage you to embrace these practices and see how they can enrich your
life.

Module 8: Dealing with Challenges
Welcome to Module 8!
In the previous module, we talked about growing spiritually and deepening your faith through daily
devotions, Bible study, and finding ways to grow closer to God.
In this module, we’re going to be talking about something we all face—challenges. Life is full of ups and
downs, and while challenges can be tough, they also give us a chance to grow stronger in our faith and
as individuals.
We are going to look at how we can face these obstacles head-on and even grow from them.
Let’s get right into it.
Facing Tough Times
Let’s start by talking about how to face tough times.
We all have those moments where life feels overwhelming. Maybe it’s the weight of financial struggles,
health concerns, or just the daily stress of managing a home.
These tough times can really test us. But, as women of faith, we’re called to see our challenges
differently.
James 1:2-4 tells us to "count it all joy when we fall into various trials," because these trials are working
on our patience and building our character.
To be honest—it’s not easy to stay joyful when you’re knee-deep in a tough situation.
I know I’ve had moments where I’m just trying to get through the day, and everything seems to be out to
steal my joy, but thanks to the Holy Spirit, I remain joyful, and I start saying, “Thank you Jesus” and
before I know it everything starts working out.
But here’s the thing—when we look back on those tough times, we often see how they shaped us.
Maybe they made us more patient, or maybe they deepened our trust in God. The challenges we face
aren’t just there to knock us down; they’re there to build us up, even when it doesn’t feel like it at the
moment.
Think back to a time when you were really struggling. Maybe it was when the kids were sick, or you were
dealing with a financial crisis, or maybe it was just one of those days when everything seemed to go
wrong.
It probably felt like too much to handle at the time, but looking back, you might see how that experience
made you stronger. It’s in those moments of struggle that we often find our faith growing the most.


Finding Support
Sometimes, it feels like you’re carrying the weight of the world alone. But God never meant for us to
handle everything by ourselves.
Ecclesiastes 4:9-10 reminds us that "two are better than one" because if one falls, the other can help
them up. We need each other—whether it’s our friends, our family, or our church community.
I remember a time when I was feeling completely overwhelmed—juggling the needs of my young kids,
trying to keep the house in order, and just feeling like I was constantly on the edge of losing it.
I thought I had to do it all on my own. But then, I reached out to a close friend. We prayed together, and
she shared some of her own struggles with me.
Just knowing I wasn’t alone, that someone else understood what I was going through, made all the
difference. It didn’t solve all my problems, but it gave me the strength to keep going.
If you’re going through something tough right now, don’t hesitate to reach out to someone. Sometimes,
just talking to someone who gets it can make all the difference. And remember, God has placed people
in your life to help you carry your burdens.
Adapting to Change
Change is hard, isn’t it?
Life with young children is especially full of changes. Just when you think you’ve got a routine down,
something shifts—maybe nap times change, or you’re suddenly dealing with a new challenge you didn’t
see coming. It can be exhausting trying to keep up.
But here’s what I’ve learned: adapting to change is part of building resilience. It’s about learning to roll
with the punches and trusting that God is guiding you through each season.
Romans 8:28 is a verse I lean on often: "And we know that all things work together for good to them
that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose."
Even when things don’t go as planned, God is working everything out for our good.
I’ve had to remind myself of this many times. Whether it’s adjusting to a new routine with the kids or
facing unexpected challenges, I’ve learned that change, though uncomfortable, is an opportunity to trust
God more and to grow in ways I might not have otherwise.
Take a look at the story of Joseph in the Bible. Joseph faced many challenges—his brothers sold him into
slavery, he was wrongly accused, and he spent years in prison. Yet, he adapted to each situation and
remained faithful to God.
In the end, Joseph’s resilience helped him become a powerful leader and save many lives. His story
shows us that even when things are tough, adapting with faith can lead to amazing outcomes.


Using Setbacks for Growth
No one ever prays to have a setback, but they happen.
They can feel like failures, but they don’t have to keep us down. In fact, some of the best growth
happens after a setback. When we hit a roadblock, we have a choice: we can let it defeat us, or we can
use it as a stepping stone to move forward.
Think about a time when something didn’t go as planned. Maybe it was a project you were working on, a
goal you were trying to achieve, or even a relationship that faced some challenges.
It’s easy to get discouraged, but if you look closely, there’s often a lesson to be learned in those
moments.
I remember trying to start a small project at home. I was so excited about it, but things didn’t go the way
I had hoped.
At first, I was really discouraged. But then I realized that the setback was showing me areas where I
needed to grow and approach things differently.
Proverbs 24:16 encourages us: "For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again." Even when we
fall, we can get back up and keep moving forward.
Setbacks are not the end of the road. They’re a part of the journey. So, when you face a setback, don’t
let it stop you. Instead, ask yourself what you can learn from it and how you can use it to grow stronger
in your faith and as a person.
Practical Strategies
Now, let’s talk about some ways to handle challenges.
a). Stress Management
First up is stress management. We all know how stressful life can get, especially when you’re balancing
so much. One of the simplest things you can do is take a moment to breathe.
It sounds so basic, but when you’re in the middle of a stressful situation, pausing to take a few deep
breaths can help calm your mind and body.
Another thing that helps is prayer. It doesn’t have to be a long, formal prayer—just a quick conversation
with God, telling Him what’s on your mind.
Philippians 4:6-7 says, "Be careful for nothing; but in everything by prayer and supplication with
thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all
understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
There have been so many times when I’ve felt overwhelmed, and just taking a moment to pray and hand
it over to God has brought me peace that I couldn’t find anywhere else.


b). Seeking Help
Another strategy is knowing when to seek help. Sometimes, we feel like we have to do everything on our
own, but that’s not true.
There’s nothing wrong with reaching out for support—whether it’s asking a friend to help with the kids,
talking to a mentor, or seeking professional advice.
Remember, it’s okay to ask for help. We all need it at times, and God has placed people in our lives to
support us. Don’t be afraid to lean on them when you need to.
Questions to Think About
As you work through your challenges, here are a few questions to consider:
 What challenges are you facing, and how can your faith help you overcome them? Reflect on
how your faith can provide strength and guidance in difficult times.
 How can past setbacks make you stronger? Think about how previous challenges have helped
you grow and what you’ve learned from them.
Action Steps
Here are a few things you can do:
 Reflect on a recent challenge and how you handled it. What did you learn from it?
 Identify a current challenge and plan how to approach it with faith and resilience.
 Reach out to someone you trust and share what you’re going through. Don’t carry the burden
alone.
Remember, facing challenges with faith doesn’t mean you won’t have hard times, but it means you have
the strength and support of God to get through them.
Embrace these moments as opportunities to grow and rely on the community around you. Each
challenge is a chance to draw closer to God and become stronger in your faith.
Thank you for joining me in this module. I hope these insights help you manage challenges with grace
and faith.
In the next module, we’ll be talking about how to recognize and celebrate your achievements, reflect on
how far you’ve come, and use your successes to inspire others and set new goals.
Stay tuned!
Quiz Yourself
1). What is a good way to handle obstacles and tough times?
A) Ignore them and hope they go away
B) See them as chances to grow and learn

C) Complain about them to everyone
2). How can you build resilience when dealing with challenges?
A) Give up when things get hard
B) Adapt to changes and use setbacks for growth
C) Refuse to change and stay stuck

3). What should you do if you need help during difficult times?
A) Seek support from friends, family, or faith groups
B) Keep your problems to yourself
C) Try to handle everything on your own

4). What is a good way to manage stress?
A) Taking on more responsibilities
B) Ignoring your feelings
C) Using techniques like meditation or deep breathing

5). What should you consider when facing a setback?
A) Give up and try something else
B) Look for opportunities to learn and grow
C) Blame others for your failure
Module 9: Celebrating Your Successes
Welcome to Module 9!
In the previous module, we tackled how to handle challenges and build resilience through tough times.
We talked about how setbacks can help us grow and how important it is to find support when we need
it.
In this module, we’re shifting gears to focus on celebrating your successes. It’s so easy to get caught up
in the next task or goal that we forget to take a moment and appreciate how far we’ve come.
We’re going to talk about how to recognize and celebrate your achievements and why doing so is so
important.


Recognizing Achievements
Celebrating your wins is a vital part of staying motivated. It’s essential to acknowledge your
accomplishments, whether they are large or small. Every success, no matter the size, deserves
recognition.
Remember Psalm 126:3, which says, “The Lord hath done great things for us; whereof we are glad.”
This verse reminds us that acknowledging the blessings and achievements in our lives brings joy and
gratitude.
When you achieve a goal or complete a task, take a moment to celebrate. This could be as simple as
treating yourself to something special or taking time to reflect on your success.
Reflect on the last time you celebrated a win. It could be finishing a long-term project, reaching a
personal goal, or even just managing to get through a challenging day. Celebrating these moments helps
build your confidence and encourages you to keep pushing forward.
Reflecting on Progress
Sometimes, we’re so focused on what’s next that we forget to appreciate how far we’ve come. Reflecting
on your progress helps you see the distance you’ve traveled and the growth you’ve achieved.
Take time to look back on your journey.
How have you grown?
What challenges have you overcome?
Reflecting on these questions can help you appreciate your achievements and build confidence for
future endeavors.
Reflecting on your progress also aligns with the encouragement from James 1:2-4, which says, “My
brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your
faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire,
wanting nothing.”
This verse highlights that trials lead to growth, and recognizing how far you’ve come is part of
celebrating that growth.
Sharing Success
Sharing your success can be really uplifting, both for you and for others. When you share your
achievements, you not only celebrate your own wins but also inspire and encourage those around you.
Think about how you can share your success. You might talk about it with friends, post about it on social
media, or write a blog post.
Your story can motivate others who are facing their own challenges. Proverbs 27:17 says, “Iron
sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.” Sharing your successes can help
strengthen and inspire those around you.

Using Success to Grow
Every success you achieve is a chance to grow. Don’t just stop at celebrating—use your achievements to
set new goals. Each win helps build your confidence and prepares you for future challenges.
Consider how you can use your success to motivate yourself for the next steps. Whether it’s setting a
new personal goal, starting a new project, or tackling a new challenge, your achievements can be a
powerful source of motivation.
Philippians 3:14 says, “I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.”
This verse encourages us to keep moving forward and striving for new goals.
Practical Actions
Here are some practical ways to celebrate and share your successes:
a). Celebration Plans
Plan a small celebration for your achievements. It doesn’t have to be big—maybe just a special treat, a
fun outing, or a quiet evening to enjoy your success.
b). Sharing Your Journey
Think about sharing your success story with others. You could write about it, talk about it with friends, or
post it on social media. Sharing your journey can offer hope and encouragement to others who might be
facing their own struggles.
Questions to Think About
Before we move on, take a moment to think about these questions:
 What achievements are you most proud of?
 How can celebrating your successes help you in the future?
Reflecting on these questions can help you understand the importance of celebrating your wins and how
it can positively impact your future goals.
Action Steps
Here are a couple of action steps to take:
 Celebrate your recent accomplishments with a special activity or treat. Enjoy and appreciate
your achievements, no matter how big or small.
 Share your success story with friends or a community group. Use your experiences to inspire and
encourage others.
That’s all for module 9!
Remember, celebrating your successes is not just about acknowledging what you’ve done; it’s also about
reinforcing your confidence and setting the stage for future growth.
By taking the time to celebrate and reflect, you’re not only honoring your achievements but also paving
the way for even more successes in the future.

As we wrap up Module 9, get ready for our final module, “Living Your Faith Daily.”
In our next session, we’ll talk about how to incorporate your faith into your everyday life, from starting
and ending your day with prayer to living out your Christian values in all you do.
Keep celebrating your wins, and get ready to take your faith into your daily routines. See you in the next
module!
Quiz Yourself
1). Why is it important to celebrate your achievements?
A. It helps you appreciate your progress and stay motivated.
B. It makes you appear boastful to others.
C. It prevents you from setting new goals.

2). How can reflecting on your progress benefit you?
A. It helps you forget about past challenges.
B. It builds confidence and helps you appreciate your growth.
C. It leads to complacency and lack of motivation.

3). What is one way to share your success with others?
A. Keep it private and only celebrate alone.
B. Post about it on social media or share it with friends.
C. Ignore it and focus on future goals.

4). How can celebrating your successes help you in the future?
A. It makes you less likely to set new goals.
B. It provides motivation and confidence to tackle new challenges.
C. It distracts you from your responsibilities.

5). What is a practical action you can take to celebrate your achievements?
A. Plan a small celebration or treat yourself to something enjoyable.
B. Ignore your success and focus solely on what’s next.

C. Avoid sharing your success with anyone.
Module 10: Living Your Faith Daily
Welcome to our final module! We've covered a lot of ground together, and it's been an amazing journey.
Now, let’s talk about bringing your faith into your everyday life.
It’s one thing to talk about faith on Sundays or when you’re at church, but how do you bring that faith
into your daily life?
How do you make sure that your Christian values shine through in everything you do?
Living your faith daily is about weaving your faith into every part of your life. This means starting and
ending your day with prayer, letting your Christian values guide your actions, and finding ways to balance
faith with your daily responsibilities.
In this module, we’ll cover some practical ways to weave faith into your daily routines, balance your
spiritual life with your everyday responsibilities, and set faith-based goals.
We’ll also talk about how to serve others as a reflection of your faith. By the end of this module, you’ll
have some great ideas for making your faith a living, breathing part of your everyday life.
Incorporating Faith into Daily Life
Starting and ending your day with prayer and devotion is a great way to keep your faith central in your
life.
I know life can be busy—between family, work, and personal commitments, finding time for prayer might
seem tough. But even a few moments of prayer can be incredibly grounding.
1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 reminds us, "Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all
circumstances."
This isn’t just about praying when things are going well but making prayer a constant part of your life.
When you wake up, take a moment to thank God for the new day and ask for His guidance. At night,
reflect on the day—thank Him for your blessings and seek help with any concerns you might have.
For example, if you're feeling overwhelmed by your to-do list, rather than rushing into your tasks, take a
moment to pray for calm and focus. It’s amazing how a simple prayer can shift your perspective and help
you tackle your tasks with a more peaceful mindset.
Living your values is another important aspect. Colossians 3:17 says, "Whatever you do, whether in
word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus."
This means letting your Christian values guide everything you do. Ask yourself, "How would Jesus handle
this?"
It’s a powerful way to make sure your daily actions align with your faith.

For instance, if you find yourself in a disagreement, approach it with love and patience, reflecting values
of forgiveness and understanding.
Balancing Faith with Daily Responsibilities
Balancing your faith with daily responsibilities is very important. Integrating faith into your home life is a
good place to start.
Ephesians 5:25 says, "Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up
for her."
This verse reminds us that love and respect should guide our family life. Even with busy schedules and
challenges, strive to show patience, kindness, and respect.
If you’re feeling frustrated with family demands, take a moment to pray for patience and a loving heart.
Your faith can help you handle these situations with grace and understanding.
At work, let your faith influence your approach. Proverbs 16:3 says, "Commit to the Lord whatever you
do, and he will establish your plans."
This means giving your best at work, treating others with respect, and handling challenges with faith. It’s
about reflecting your values in your interactions with colleagues.
For example, if you’re dealing with a difficult coworker, try approaching the situation with empathy and a
spirit of cooperation guided by your faith.
Practical Faith-Based Actions
Setting faith goals can help keep your spiritual life on track. Proverbs 3:6 says, "In all your ways submit
to him, and he will make your paths straight."
Think about setting goals that reflect your spiritual and personal growth. Maybe you want to deepen
your Bible study, increase your prayer time, or get more involved in church activities. These goals help
keep your faith central in your daily life.
For instance, if you set a goal to read a chapter of the Bible every day, you might find this daily habit
helps you stay focused and grounded in your faith.
Engaging in acts of charity and service is another way to live out your faith. Matthew 25:40 tells us,
"Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for
me."
Look for opportunities to serve others in your community, whether it’s volunteering at a local shelter,
helping a neighbor, or supporting a charity. These acts not only help those in need but also strengthen
your own spiritual connection.
Consider joining a community service project at your church or organizing a charity drive. It’s a practical
way to show love and support for others while living out your faith.


Questions to Think About
 How can you start your day with a focus on faith? Think about practical ways to include prayer or
Bible reading in your morning routine. What small changes can you make to start your day with a
mindset of faith?
 In what ways can you reflect your values in your daily activities? Reflect on how you can let your
Christian values guide your actions and decisions throughout the day. What are some specific
ways you can make your faith visible in everyday moments?
Action Steps
 Create a Daily Routine: Design a routine that includes time for prayer, Bible reading, and
reflection. It doesn’t have to be long, just consistent. Set aside a specific time each day—
whether in the morning or evening—to stay connected to your faith amidst your busy life.
 Identify a Charity or Community Service Opportunity: Find ways to get involved in your
community. Look for a cause that resonates with you and see how you can contribute your time
and talents. Volunteering or supporting a charity can be a meaningful way to live out your faith
and make a difference in the lives of others.
As we wrap up this module—and our journey together—remember that living your faith daily involves
making small, intentional choices that reflect your values and beliefs.
It’s about weaving faith into every part of your life, balancing spiritual and personal responsibilities, and
finding ways to serve others.
Your faith isn’t just for Sundays; it can guide you through every part of your life. By setting faith-based
goals, seeking service opportunities, and making prayer and devotion daily habits, you’re creating a life
that truly reflects your deepest values and beliefs.
I want to congratulate you because you have done an amazing job coming this far and completing this
course, and I hope you feel empowered and ready to live out your transformation.
As you embrace your journey, remember that growth is an ongoing process.
Stay open to learning and evolving, and trust that God is with you every step of the way.
You are not alone; your experiences can inspire others to seek their path of growth and transformation.
Keep moving forward, knowing that you are loved, supported, and empowered to live a fulfilling life in
Christ.
Thank you for joining me on this journey. I hope you’ve found inspiration and practical advice to help you
live a faith-filled life.
May your days be blessed with peace, joy, and a deep sense of God’s presence in every moment.
God bless you as you continue your journey of faith and growth.

Quiz Yourself
1). What is one key practice for integrating faith into daily life?
A) Establishing a daily routine that includes prayer and reflection
B) Attending church services regularly
C) Participating in community events

2). Which of the following is a suggested way to demonstrate faith in your interactions with others?
A) Showing kindness and compassion
B) Prioritizing your own needs
C) Ignoring conflicts

3). What role does gratitude play in living out your faith daily?
A) It distracts from daily tasks
B) It enhances overall well-being and perspective
C) It is only necessary during difficult times

4). How can you effectively manage challenges and setbacks in your daily life as part of your faith
journey?
A) By relying solely on your own strength
B) By avoiding difficult situations
C) By seeking support from your faith community and prayer

5). What is a simple way to share your faith with others throughout the day?
A) Living out your values and being a positive example
B) Engaging in lengthy debates about beliefs
C) Keeping your beliefs private to avoid conflicts

Video Script Title:
"I Thought I Knew Everything"

Scene 1: Living Room – Quiet Morning

Adaora, 42, sits on the couch, dressed, a WhatsApp message notification pops up.

She opens it and reads silently. Her face softens.

On-screen close-up of her phone:
"Saw this and thought it might help you the way you help all of us."
Attached are screenshots from an article titled "Understanding Changes in Your Menstrual Cycle After 40."

Adaora scrolls through a few short excerpts:

  • "It's normal for menstrual cycles to become irregular as you approach menopause."
  • "Hormonal shifts can cause heavier or longer periods."
  • "Tracking your symptoms helps you understand your body better."

Scene 2: Curious, She Replies
Typing slowly, she sends:
"Thank you. I've been feeling confused. I'll check out the app."

Scene 3: Exploring Cyclekits

Cut to Adaora opening the Google Play Store and downloading the Cyclekits app.

She taps through:

Scene 4: Adaora (softly, to herself):
"A platform for Nigerian women...
Period tracking, health education, and nurses I can talk to...
Even discreet period care delivered to my door?"

She shakes her head slightly, smiling with quiet surprise. For the first time, she looks... understood.

Scene 5: That Evening

Her husband walks in from work. She looks up from her phone.

Adaora:
"I downloaded the app... and it's actually good. It's like it was made for women like me."

Husband (smiling):
"Then I'm glad. I will help you pay for the subscription."

Adaora is visibly touched.

Scene 6: The Next Morning – Delivery

Doorbell rings. Adaora opens the door and receives a simple brown box.

She places it on the table and opens it slowly. Inside: trusted pad brands, wipes, panty liners, and a small note: "For every stage of your journey."

She touches the items gently, her expression one of calm and care.

Scene 7: Closing Scene

Back on the couch, Adaora scrolls through the app again to read another article, her husband seated beside her.

Adaora (quietly):
"I didn't know how much I needed this."

Husband:
"You never have to go through it alone again."

On-screen Text:
No woman should walk through this phase alone.
Track your cycle. Get answers. Access care. With Cyclekits.
www.cyclekits.ng
Real Care. For Every Phase.
